items.design:
**Status:** design settled 2026-07-01 (two Q&A rounds — see DEVLOG). Prerequisite for BL-089 (commercial-sphere fog), which reads these routes. Calls (Ben): routes **emergent** from convoy traffic (no new player verb); **one completed convoy establishes** a route; **player corp's own commerce only** need be recorded for the fog; **mild decay** — routes carry a last-traffic stamp so the reader can age them to 'stale', never deleting them.

### Why this exists
Convoys today are transient: `convoy_component` (`source_market → dest_market`, `corp`, `progress`) is auto-dispatched by `auto_dispatch` to fill a shortfall and **retired on arrival** (`credit_arrived_convoys` erases it) — `world.convoys` is explicitly "no persistent identity". There is therefore **no durable lane** for a fog/visibility system to read. This item adds the missing persistent object: a **trade route** = a body-pair lane that the player's commerce has actually run. Pure trade-system data addition; the fog (BL-089) is a separate consumer.

### Data model
A route is keyed on the **body pair** (fog is body-level), not the market pair (a body may host several market centres — all collapse to the same lane for visibility):
```cpp
struct trade_route {
    entity_id body_a       = null_entity;  // the two bodies the lane connects (unordered)
    entity_id body_b       = null_entity;
    entity_id corp         = null_entity;  // dispatching corp (fog reads player's only; stored for generality)
    int       last_tick    = 0;            // sim tick a convoy last COMPLETED this lane — drives stale-aging in BL-089
    int       convoy_count = 0;            // cumulative completions (telemetry / future volume model)
};
```
Held in `world.trade_routes` (a `std::vector`, mirroring `world.convoys`). A route, once created, is **never erased** by this item — aging to 'stale' is a *read-time* concern owned by BL-089 (freshness = `now − last_tick`), so no deletion logic and no flicker.

### Population (the one hook into the trade system)
When a convoy completes — in `credit_arrived_convoys`, at the point the convoy is credited and about to be erased — **upsert its route** before erasing the convoy:
- Resolve the convoy's `source_market`/`dest_market` to their owning **bodies** (needs `body_of_market(const world&, entity_id market)` — add if absent; markets already know their body via `market_component`).
- Find-or-insert the `trade_route` for that unordered `(body_a, body_b)` pair **and** `corp`; set `last_tick = current sim tick`; `++convoy_count`.
- Recording **all** corps' completions is acceptable (cheap), but the fog only reads `corp == player`. Simplest correct scope: record player-corp convoys at minimum; recording all future-proofs rival-route reveals (deferred).
- Skip degenerate lanes where source and dest resolve to the **same body** (intra-body convoys light nothing).

### 'Active' lanes (live traffic) — derived, not stored
BL-089's *Visible* tier needs "a convoy is currently in transit on this lane". That is **derived on demand** from the live `world.convoys` vector (any convoy whose endpoints resolve to this body-pair and `corp == player`), not stored on the route — live convoys are the source of truth for 'active', the route record is the source of truth for 'has ever run / last ran'. Keeps the two concerns from drifting.

### Determinism, serialisation, scope
- **Deterministic:** population is driven entirely by deterministic convoy completions + the sim tick counter. No RNG, no Lua, no per-tile exposure.
- **Serialisation seam:** `world.trade_routes` **joins the flat-binary read+write paths symmetrically** when that path exists (as flagged for `survey_state` in BL-067 — currently no save/load is wired in `world/*`; flag at integration so routes are not silently dropped from a future snapshot). Aging is derived, so no freshness field needs saving beyond `last_tick`.
- **Scope:** data + population only. **No rendering, no fog, no new player verb** — all of that is BL-089. Done when routes accumulate correctly and survive a completion cycle.

### Requirements (Full mode)
- **`headless`** — a `tools/verify/trade_routes_*.cpp` harness: a completed player convoy upserts exactly one route for the correct body-pair with `last_tick` = completion tick; a second convoy on the same lane bumps `convoy_count` and `last_tick` without duplicating; an intra-body convoy records nothing; `body_of_market` resolves a market to its body. No visual requirement (nothing renders here).

### Deferred extensions
Rival-route recording surfaced to the player (waits on rivals acting — standing AI-stub rule); cumulative-volume or sustained-traffic thresholds (Ben chose one-convoy-establishes; the `convoy_count` field leaves room); directional routes / lane capacity.

items.title: Commercial-sphere visibility — route-driven three-level activity fog (Unknown/Known/Visible)
items.summary: The player's trade network is their intelligence network: where goods flow, the map lights up, radiating from the player's own commerce. A body-level three-level ACTIVITY fog (Unknown/Known/Visible+stale) driven by BL-088 routes + presence, INDEPENDENT of the geographic survey fog (BL-067). Corridor + proximity-glow illumination on the Solar canvas; Known reveals a coarse market pulse, not internals. Completes the v0.0.8 Discovery theme.
items.design:
**Status:** design settled 2026-07-01 (two Q&A rounds — see DEVLOG). `requires` BL-088 (persistent trade routes). Calls (Ben): a **three-level activity fog** (Unknown / Known / Visible) **independent of** the shipped survey system (BL-067) — survey is the *geographic* fog (tiles/deposits), this is the *activity* fog (market pulse, presence); **player commerce is the only light source**; **corridor + proximity glow** illumination (routing past a body reveals it); **Known reveals a market pulse + coarse activity**, not internals; a Known body decays to **stale** (greyed, never back to Unknown); **Visible** = an active lane OR a building present.

### The idea in one line
The player's trade network is their intelligence network: **where your goods flow, the world lights up**, radiating from your own activity so growth opens the map. Fog keeps the spotlight on the player and makes commercial reach *felt*, rather than simulating corporate secrecy (explicitly rejected as too sim-like).

### Two fogs, layered (not chained)
Ben chose **independent axes**, so this system does **not** gate or replace survey:
| Fog | Owns | Driver | Grain |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Geographic** (shipped: BL-067 survey, BL-068 markers) | tiles, deposit bands, **individual rival building markers** | player dispatches a survey | per-tile / per-region |
| **Activity** (THIS item) | body-level Unknown/Known/Visible, market pulse, coarse activity | player trade routes (BL-088) + presence | per-body |
A body can be **Known** (a route reaches it → you read its market and activity) yet **unsurveyed** (no tiles, and per BL-068 no individual rival markers). The two states render as **separate badges** on the Solar canvas and must be visually distinguishable (integration concern below). BL-068's per-building rival markers stay **survey-gated**, unchanged; this item adds only a coarser body-level read on top.

### Per-body activity state (derived, pure function)
`body_activity_visibility(const world&, entity_id body) -> activity_vis` computed on demand from routes + convoys + ownership (no stored state, no serialisation):
```cpp
enum class activity_vis : uint8_t { unknown, known_stale, known, visible };
```
- **visible** — an **active** player lane touches the body (a live `player` convoy in transit on a route with this endpoint) **OR** the player owns a building on it. Live, current feed.
- **known** — a player `trade_route` has this body as an endpoint **and** `now − route.last_tick ≤ route_fresh_ticks`.
- **known_stale** — a player route endpoint exists but `now − last_tick > route_fresh_ticks`. Greyed, "last seen N days ago". **Never** returns to `unknown` (mild-decay call).
- **unknown** — none of the above: a public astronomy dot only (type + orbital position + grid size — exactly BL-067's pre-survey read).
`home_body` and any body the player starts with a building on begin **visible**; all else **unknown** (independent of survey state, which BL-067 already seeds).

### Illumination geometry (corridor + proximity glow)
Rendered on the **Solar canvas** (`solar_system_canvas.cpp`), where routes and bodies live:
- **Endpoints** — each player-route endpoint body renders at its activity state (badges below).
- **Corridor** — a lit line/arc between the two endpoint bodies' current positions for **active** lanes (soft glow along the lane; faded for stale routes). Purely visual.
- **Proximity glow (the 'peek')** — when a player convoy **completes** a lane, sample body positions **at that completion tick** and mark any body whose closest approach to the endpoint segment is within radius `R` as **known_stale** (a faint, decaying glimpse). This is the "route past a frontier body to reveal it" mechanic, made **discrete and deterministic** (one sample at a discrete tick; positions are a pure function of tick — no per-frame state, no flicker, no RNG). `R` and the freshness window are **calibration constants** (headless-tuned). *(Chosen over a per-frame proximity test, which would depend on live orbital drift and flicker.)*

### What 'Known' reveals (coarse — strategy read, not sim readout)
On a Known/Visible body, the Selection panel and hover surface a **market pulse**: the body's public market (prices, supply/demand — already public per BL-068) plus a coarse **activity level** (busy ◉◉◉○○ / quiet), derived from public market throughput. **No** per-building detail, production, or stockpiles (those stay BL-068-private / survey-gated). Unknown bodies show only type + position; stale bodies show the last-seen pulse, greyed with an age.

### UI surfaces
- **Solar canvas** — per-body **activity badge** distinct from BL-067's survey badge: `unknown` dimmed dot; `known` crisp with a small market-pulse pip; `known_stale` greyed + age; `visible` a live indicator. Corridor + proximity glow as above. New glyph(s) in `ui::icons` per ICONS.md; state colours in `presentation.hpp`.
- **Selection panel** (`selection_panel.cpp`) — a body panel gains an **activity section** keyed on `activity_vis`: unknown → "Outside your network — no market data"; known/visible → market pulse + activity; known_stale → greyed last-seen. Composes with the Survey section (BL-067) and body summary.
- **Hover** (`hover_content.cpp`) — body hover shows name/type always; market pulse only when known+.

### Determinism, serialisation, scope
- **Deterministic & derived:** activity state is a pure function of `trade_routes` + `convoys` + ownership + tick; **nothing new is serialised** (routes are serialised by BL-088; the proximity-glimpse marks, if persisted, ride on a `last_glimpse_tick` int on `body_component` that joins the save seam; otherwise recomputed). No Lua, no per-tile exposure.
- **Integration hotspots** (single-writer, main session): `solar_system_canvas.cpp` (badge + corridor + glow), `presentation.hpp`, `icons.{hpp,cpp}`. Reconcile the two-badge visual language with BL-067's survey badge at integration.
- **Authority doc:** the discovery/visibility model now spans BL-067/068/088/089 and outgrows a ROADMAP note — spin out a dedicated `docs/ui/DISCOVERY.md` on landing and repoint BL-067/068's `authority_doc` there.

### Requirements (Full mode)
- **`visual`** — `scripts/verify/commercial_fog.lua`: a body with no player route renders `unknown` (dot only); after a player convoy completes a lane to it, `known` with a market pulse; a stale route greyed; a body with a live lane or a player building `visible`; a frontier body near a completed lane's corridor shows the faint proximity glimpse. Golden-blessed.
- **`headless`** — `tools/verify/commercial_fog_*.cpp`: `body_activity_visibility` returns the right tier for each of {no route, fresh route, stale route, active lane, presence}; `home_body` starts visible; the state is independent of survey phase (a surveyed-but-unrouted body is still `unknown` for activity; an unsurveyed-but-routed body is `known`).

### Deferred extensions
Rival routes lit for the player (waits on rivals acting); an Opportunity-lens tie-in (BL-086) reading the fog; per-resource 'where is X cheap' inference tooling; a persistent minimap of the commercial sphere.
items.resolution: Delivered (v0.0.8, commit af07ad0). Core fog shipped and verified: activity_vis + pure body_activity_visibility (routes + live convoys + ownership + tick), Solar pulse badge (offset from the survey badge) + lit corridors, Selection-panel activity section; commercial_fog_harness 9/9 + golden. Authority spun out to docs/ui/DISCOVERY.md (commit 8d5915c) and repointed 2026-07-04. DEFERRALS (both lifted into standalone items on merge to main 2026-07-05): (1) the hover-card body activity line = BL-100, DELIVERED in the v0.0.9 batch (2026-07-05) — the Solar body tooltip now carries a short activity read (solar_system_canvas.cpp). (2) The deterministic proximity 'glimpse' peek = BL-099, REMAINS DEFERRED — it needs either a serialised last_glimpse_tick on body_component (save-seam change) or orbital back-computation from the mutated orbital_angle_rad; disproportionate determinism/serialisation risk for a polish minor. Re-assess at the v0.1.0 boundary; see DISCOVERY.md § Deferred extensions.

items.design:

`profile_panel_width` is a fixed 200px constant; long generated nation names overflow the 'Parent:' line and clip at the panel edge. Cosmetic, but it undercuts the identity read the card was just given.

items.design:
**Status:** designed — follow-up to the QOL framing pass.

### Problem
The start framing centres on the centroid of the player's buildings and every owned tile gets the same wash+ring, so there is no single anchor that says 'HQ here'. A headquarters marker gives the player a home base to orient from.

### Approach
- Pick the HQ tile deterministically (the player's first/primary building on the home body; revisit if an explicit HQ concept is added to the data model later).
- Draw a distinct HQ glyph (a small star/pennant, or the corp emblem from BL-090 at a larger size) over that tile, above the ordinary building marker, independent of lens.
- Optionally retarget the start-framing centroid to the HQ tile specifically once it exists.

### Notes
Composes with BL-090 (corp emblem) — the cleanest HQ marker is the corp's own emblem enlarged on the HQ tile. Keep it lens-independent like the ownership ring.

items.title: Selection element redesign — action-first surface + lens strip relocated to the minimap
items.summary: Playtest finding (2026-07-04, Ben): the Selection element has no clear purpose — it reads as an amalgamation of all the menu ledgers (a 50/50 stat-block | lens-supplement split, uniform flat text, a dead placeholder portrait) and is too cramped in its bottom-bar form. Redesign it as a strict ACTION SURFACE answering one question — 'what's my move here?' — with the kind's primary affordance dominant, only decision-relevant facts, and all reference detail pushed to the ledgers. Reclaims screen space by relocating the lens control strip onto the minimap.
items.design:
**Status:** designed — settled 2026-07-04 with Ben over a four-call Q&A (remit / lens-supplement / form / lens-trim). Full mode (multi-file UI: selection panel rewrite + layout geometry + overlay controls + minimap chrome).

### The problem (diagnosed against the live code)
The Selection element (`draw_selection_panel`, `src/ui/selection_panel.cpp`) today is a pinned bottom bar: a placeholder portrait box, then a **50/50 split** — `draw_summary` (encyclopedic stat block) on the left, `draw_lens_supplement` + the kind's affordance on the right. Three faults make it read as 'an amalgamation of all menu ledgers' and obscure its purpose: (1) facts and actions carry **equal weight**, so the affordance — the panel's whole reason to exist — has no primacy; (2) `draw_lens_supplement` (overlay-keyed market price / production rate / population-workforce rows) **literally re-renders ledger content inline**, duplicating the Market/Production/Population ledgers; (3) everything is **uniform flat text**, so a survey *button* looks identical to an orbit *fact*. It is also too short in the fixed bottom-bar height to show its content.

### The principle (Ben's framing)
The Selection element answers exactly one question: **'what's my move here?'** It is the *opposite* of a ledger — a ledger is exhaustive reference reached deliberately from the rail; this is a decision prompt that appears when you click. So: **one primary affordance per selection kind, visually dominant; a slim identity line; only the facts that inform that decision; a `go to` for the deep ledger.**

### Calls settled (Ben)
1. **Remit — action surface (aggressive).** The primary affordance dominates; keep only facts that inform that one decision; ALL reference detail (orbit, parent, composition, deposits, prices) moves to the ledgers, reached via `go to`.
2. **Lens supplement — cut entirely.** Remove `draw_lens_supplement`. Market/production/population detail is the ledgers' job; the active lens already tints the map and `go to` opens the right ledger.
3. **Form — cut the bottom bar; relocate.** The current bottom-bar form is too small. The **lens control strip moves onto the minimap** (bottom-right), reprising the pre-BL-013 minimap mode-bar location; the selection element **drops down to own the whole bottom-left corner** (nav-rail edge → minimap's left edge, top → the very bottom margin), reclaiming the ~40px strip band + bottom margin so the action content has real vertical room.
4. **Lens trim — single row of 7.** 9 glyphs do not fit the 240px minimap. Keep a single row of **Corp, Country, Resource, Market, Population, Opportunity, Production**; move **Scarcity + Industry** to keyboard-cycle only (joining Supply, already off-strip). The 140px resource/good combo (Resource/Market/Scarcity lenses) does not fit inline on the minimap bar → it becomes a small **popup** opened from the bar.

### New selection-element structure (per kind)
- **Header:** `[entity icon] Name · type   [Go to] [×]` — a real entity icon (corp emblem / body glyph / building marker / settlement) replaces the placeholder rectangle.
- **Hero — the one primary action, dominant:**
  - **Tile →** Build (the buildable-types front door + cost, affordability-gated — today's `draw_build_front_door`, promoted to the star; the BL-071 Thrives/Valid affordance read stays as its supporting fact).
  - **Body →** Dispatch Survey (`hidden`) · progress (`in_transit`/`scanning`) · Go to surface (`surveyed`).
  - **Building (player) →** **Manage ▸** — routes to the building-management surface (`construction_panel.cpp`, which already owns the workforce slider / recipe / decommission); the selection element does not duplicate those controls.
  - **Building (rival) →** no action — 'intel only', owner name (competitor internals stay private, BL-068).
  - **Market / Unit / Nation / Corporation →** their `go to` / ledger route (stubbed as today).
- **Facts — one slim, muted line, decision-relevant only:** tile → Thrives: <resources> · balance; survey → cost · ETA; building → Net/tick ✓/✗ (from `estimate_building_profit`, kept — it is a decision fact, not a ledger); body(surveyed) → the BL-089 activity pulse.
- **Cut from the panel:** `draw_lens_supplement`, and the encyclopedic `draw_*_summary` stat blocks (demoted to the header identity line; full detail lives in the Tile/Market/Balance ledgers via `go to`).

### Files & seams
- `selection_panel.cpp` — rewrite `draw_selection_panel` (header+hero+facts); drop `draw_lens_supplement`; the survey/activity/profit/affordance/front-door helpers are reused, re-laid-out. Entity icon in the header via `ui::icons` + `presentation.hpp` (corp emblem reuses the BL-090 shape hash if promoted, else the profile-card helper).
- `overlay.{cpp,hpp}` — `draw_overlay_controls` becomes the minimap mode bar: trim `modes[]` to the 7; the resource selector → a popup; positioned by the minimap block.
- `app.cpp` — minimap block draws the 7-lens mode bar (adds a bar row to the minimap chrome); remove the bottom-left `draw_overlay_controls` call; reposition `draw_selection_panel` to the full bottom-left (bottom_y = disp.y − margin, taller height, no `overlay_strip_h` offset).
- Scarcity/Industry keyboard-cycle: retain their `overlay_mode` + keyboard toggle; they simply leave the on-screen strip (LENSES.md notes them as keyboard-only, like Supply).

### Requirement (Full mode)
- **`visual`** — a `scripts/verify/selection_redesign.lua` capture set: (a) a selected **tile** shows the Build hero + Thrives/balance fact, no stat block, no lens supplement; (b) a selected **unsurveyed body** shows the Dispatch Survey hero; (c) a selected **player building** shows Manage ▸ + Net/tick fact; (d) the **minimap** shows the 7-lens mode bar and the bottom-left no longer carries a separate lens strip; (e) the selection element occupies the full bottom-left corner. Golden-blessed.

### Authority propagation (on landing)
SELECTION.md (the element's remit + per-kind hero/facts, replacing the stat-block polymorphism table), LAYOUT.md (bottom-left = selection element full-height; lens strip removed; minimap hosts the lens bar), MINIMAP.md (the lens mode bar returns to the minimap), LENSES.md (strip relocated to the minimap; Scarcity + Industry now keyboard-only, like Supply; the 7-lens on-screen set).
items.resolution: Delivered. Action surface shipped: header ([kind icon] name · type · [>][x]) + Action | Facts columns; tile→Build front door + affordances, body→Survey/Go-to-surface + activity, player building→Manage building (routes to construction panel) + profitability, rival→intel only. draw_summary + draw_lens_supplement removed (selection_panel.cpp). Lens strip relocated to a 7-glyph minimap mode bar (overlay.cpp draw_overlay_controls(x,top_y,w); app.cpp minimap block); Scarcity+Industry keyboard-only; resource selector → popup. Selection element owns the bottom-left corner, sized to content in text-line units per kind (resolution-robust — fixes the mm_h-pinned expansion Ben hit at 1920x1080; startup display log + DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES § Display environment added). Verified: selection_redesign.lua 3 goldens blessed (Windows) + eyeball. Owed on the Linux box: re-bless the minimap-visible goldens invalidated by the lens-bar relocation. Design propagated to SELECTION/LAYOUT/MINIMAP/LENSES.

items.title: v0.2.0 player-identity pivot — nation as the strategic actor, chartered corp (prototyped as 1) as the economic one
items.summary: Concept decision, settled 2026-07-04 with Ben (three-call Q&A: identity / coupling / spine). For v0.2.0 the player pivots from corporation to NATION as the strategic actor — owning research, military, and intelligence — while the corporation stays the economic actor, prototyped as a single chartered corp (= today's player corp), so the v0.0.x economy loop survives intact and the nation is a thin strategic layer above it. Settled: (1) the player IS one of the 14 generated Voronoi nations, its broad economy staying AI-run background so the specialist loop + economic premise hold unchanged; (2) tight / shared treasury for the prototype-of-1 (the chartered corp's treasury is the nation's economic arm; tax-as-a-layer returns at 1→N); (3) Military anchors v0.2.0 first. Promotes BL-054 nation behaviour + symmetrical rules from parked to load-bearing and requires a new conflict/military design item. Designed but parked (F) — implementation is v0.2.0, promoted on the next cut; design settled ahead. Do not edit authority docs now.
items.design:
**Status:** designed — settled 2026-07-04 with Ben over a three-call Q&A (identity / coupling / spine). Resolves the long-open player-identity question in CONCEPT.md ('a corporate OR nation-state entity ... a single, committed choice once tradeoffs are weighed'). **Parked for the v0.2.0 arc** (post-v0.1.0): design is settled ahead of sequence (permitted — design may settle early; only implementation and authority-doc propagation wait for the cut).

### The decision
For v0.2.0 the player pivots from a corporation to the **nation** as the strategic actor, owning the three systems that do not sit right on a single corporation — **research, military, and intelligence**. The corporation stays the **economic** actor: the nation charters corporations, and the player-nation is **prototyped as a single chartered corp** (= today's player corp), so the entire v0.0.x economy loop survives intact and the nation is a thin strategic layer *above* it, not a re-plumb. Clean division: **nation = strategic choices (research / force / intel); chartered corp = economic choices (build / trade)** — each still justifying itself by feeding Trade or Conflict.

### Settled calls (Ben, 2026-07-04)
1. **Player identity — one of the generated nations.** The player IS one of the 14 Voronoi nations (NATION_GENERATION.md), not a bolted-on special case. Its broad industrial base stays **AI-run background** exactly as today, so the **economic premise holds unchanged** (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § The economic premise) and the player never micromanages the saturated economy. Economic agency = the chartered corp; strategic agency = the new nation layer. Because the player is the *same kind of entity* as its rivals, **symmetrical rules** (CONCEPT.md § Symmetrical rules) apply cleanly and **BL-054 nation behaviour** is promoted from background stub to first-class — every AI nation runs the same nation layer.
2. **Charter coupling — tight / shared treasury (prototype-of-1).** With a single chartered corp, the corp's treasury **is** the nation's economic arm: one linked balance funds building / trade AND research / military / intel. The corp↔nation split is therefore one of **agency layer** (which surface you act through), not of money. **1→N evolution note:** the shared treasury is a prototype-of-1 simplification; once a nation charters *multiple* corps it no longer holds, and the existing **tax-as-automated-layer** thread (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Open items) returns as the funding coupling — the nation taxes its chartered corps into a distinct national budget. Recorded so the tight choice does not ossify.
3. **v0.2.0 spine — Military.** The nation strategic layer leads with **standing forces / conflict**, not research or intel. Risk + rationale: Conflict is the **least-designed pillar** (today a data-model stub, excluded from the prototype — TECH_FOUNDATIONS), so it carries the most design risk — but it is the most distinctive Era-0 → 'WW3-scale rupture' payoff (CONCEPT.md § Eras) and the cleanest Trade→Conflict link (the nation raises and commands forces from the shared treasury; materiel is drawn from the chartered corp's production and supply lines are live targets — CONCEPT § Combat). Research (BL-087) and intelligence (the DISCOVERY.md substrate) follow in later v0.2.x minors.

### The economic-premise reconciliation (closed)
The risk flagged at capture — does elevating the player to nation-level force them to manage the broad saturated economy? — is closed by call 1: the player-nation's broad economy stays AI-run background, identical to how the 14 nations already carry it. The player still plays as a specialist through one chartered corp; the nation layer sits *above* the economy loop, it does not replace it. Premise and the 14-nation background mass both intact.

### Scope this promotes (the v0.2.0 cost)
- **BL-054 (nation behaviour)** — parked stub → load-bearing: AI nations must run the same nation layer the player does (symmetry).
- **A new conflict / military design item** — none exists today; the Military-first spine needs one authored at v0.2.0 promotion (nation force model, materiel↔production link, supply-line targeting). Conflict graduates from data-model stub to designed pillar.
- **Symmetrical rules** become load-bearing at the nation tier.

### Child items to create at v0.2.0 promotion (NOT now — avoid a parked cascade)
- Nation strategic layer + shared-treasury wiring (chartered-corp-as-economic-arm seam).
- Military / conflict design (the spine) — first subsystem.
- BL-054 promotion to playable nation behaviour.
- Research (BL-087) + intelligence re-homing — later v0.2.x.

### Authority propagation (on landing, NOT now)
CONCEPT.md (identity committed to nation-level, chartered-corp-prototyped-as-1), SYSTEMS.md (nation as the strategic layer over chartered corps; Research / Military / Intel owned at the nation tier), GENERATION_STRATEGY.md + CORPORATION_GENERATION.md (player-nation = one of the 14; chartered-corp origin; shared-treasury → tax at 1→N). Do NOT edit these now — authority time-slicing; v0.1.0 not cut.

### Delivery note
Design settled 2026-07-04 (this session); item flips design-owed → designed but stays **parked (F)** — implementation is v0.2.0, to be promoted on the next cut.

items.title: Markets hold a resource stockpile; construction draws from / is gated on the local market stock
items.summary: Idea (2026-07-04, Ben): building materials must be a real, visible constraint sourced from the MARKET, not the corp's private pool. Today construction checks the corp's `corp_body_pools` on the body (construct_building → insufficient_materials) and markets carry only supply/demand/price — no physical resource stockpile. Give markets a resource stockpile and gate/charge construction against the LOCAL market's stock, so 'you can only build where the market can supply the materials'. Prerequisite framing for BL-096 (resource-driven market generation). Material cost is already surfaced in the build front door (BL-044 clarity, 2026-07-04); this changes WHERE the materials come from. [DESIGNED 2026-07-07: derived-from-supply stock; construction rate modulated by material availability (full/stretched/paused), pay-as-you-build, construction competes as a real market buyer. Real-inventory revisit -> BL-130.]
items.design:
**Status: DESIGNED 2026-07-07** (design session, Ben).

### Market stock model — DERIVED (not a persistent inventory)
- Market 'stock' is **derived from recent supply** (a rolling/smoothed throughput figure), NOT a stored per-resource inventory. Chosen for calculation simplicity.
- **Correction to the earlier open design:** with derived stock there is **no new serialized inventory field on the flat-binary seam** and nothing extra to tick — the serialisation concern the original prose raised does not apply.
- Revisit real inventory vs derived after an optimization/efficiency pass → **BL-130**.

### Materials come from the market (already shipped — BL-095-lite)
- A building's `resource_build_cost` is bought from the local market at prevailing price and folded into the credit cost (construction.cpp) — sidesteps the empty-fresh-corp-pool deadlock. Retained.

### Construction rate modulated by material availability (the new mechanic)
- Construction is already **durative** (`ticks_remaining = build_duration_ticks`). Now **material availability modulates the drain rate**, in three regimes:
  - surplus ample → full speed (base duration)
  - surplus tight → **stretched**, up to a max (~10×; e.g. a 6-month build → 5 years max)
  - surplus below even the max-stretch rate → **paused** until it recovers
- **Pay-as-you-build**: materials are drawn and paid *incrementally* as construction progresses (entailed by the rate model — a build can only be slow-because-starved if materials arrive over time).
- Construction is a **real market buyer**: its draw adds genuine demand, competes with population and other builds, and bids up local price; a paused build stops spending. Concurrent builds genuinely contend for the derived stock.

### Front door
- The BL-071 reason-coded rejection is **upgraded from binary to analog**: show a rate/ETA ("~4yr — materials scarce") or "paused — market can't supply" instead of a hard reject.

Touches economy/construction/market seam → Full mode, determinism-sensitive. Prerequisite for BL-096. Authority → PRODUCTION.md on landing. Related: BL-078 (same substrate, supply side), BL-130 (inventory revisit).

items.title: Resource-driven market generation — markets split/dissolve by resource concentration, not land area
items.summary: Idea (2026-07-04, Ben): reframe market generation — markets are 'less to do with equal amounts of land, and more to do with splitting resources from greedy actors'. Generate markets from RESOURCE concentration: a region with too few resources has no market (one dissolves); a resource-rich region splits into multiple markets. Market count and boundaries reflect resource wealth, not land partition. Requires BL-095 (markets holding resource stockpiles) as the substrate. Ben's steer: 'generation can come afterwards' — settle BL-095 first. [DESIGNED 2026-07-07: one-pass gen; population-anchored + resource-concentration shaped; nations carve splits. Fuller co-gen -> BL-132; player market destruction -> BL-131.]
items.design:
**Status: DESIGNED 2026-07-07** (design session, Ben) — first cut scoped; fuller vision deferred to BL-132.

### First cut (this item)
- **One-pass at world-gen** — NO runtime split/merge. The generated market map is fixed for the campaign; the ONLY runtime market change is player-driven destruction → **BL-131**.
- Markets stay **population-anchored** (from the BL-078 demand model); **resource concentration shapes count/extent** — a resource-rich region fractures into more markets, a barren one folds into its neighbour.
- **Carving actors = nations** at generation time: nations exist before markets in the gen order and already tile the map (Voronoi territory + substrate density), so a resource cluster spanning two nations' territory becomes two markets. No generation reorder required.

### Deferred (out of this item)

- **BL-131** — player-driven market destruction (mechanism TBD).

items.title: Bound every shell view/panel like the Selection element — resolution-robust, content-sized
items.summary: Idea (2026-07-04, Ben): treat every view/panel the way BL-093 fixed the Selection element — properly bounded and resolution-robust. BL-093 found the Selection panel ballooned/clipped because its height was pinned to the resolution-scaled minimap height (mm_h); the fix sized it from content in text-line units. Audit the rest of the shell chrome (header, profile, nav rail, time panel, explorer, minimap, ledger windows, on-canvas keys/strips) for the same class of bug — anything pinned to a resolution-scaled dimension or another element's size, or that can clip/overflow off the verify-capture resolution (1280x720) vs the runtime window — and bound each from content + fixed shell anchors. Standing practice already recorded in DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES § Display environment; this is the sweep that applies it everywhere.
items.design:
**Status:** complete. Landed 47da542 (fix) after the read-only audit found two real bugs: time-panel height (`app.cpp`, was `mm_h*0.5f`, now sized from content in text-line units) and the Tile Ledger's stale spawn anchor (`ledger_chrome.hpp`, was seeded from the superseded `profile_panel_width=200`, now `ledger_window_spawn(disp_x)`/`ledger_window_size(disp_x,disp_y)` functions anchored off `shell_column_width` + clamped to viewport). Header/profile/nav-rail/minimap/explorer/economy-panel/lens-key audited and confirmed already correct (no fix needed). Full build clean; a `scripts/verify/*.lua` multi-resolution sweep script was not authored (candidate follow-up tool). Captured 2026-07-04 (Ben). Generalises the BL-093 fix.

### The problem class
BL-093 (Selection element) balllooned with empty space / clipped because its height was pinned to `mm_h` (`mm_w = max(240, 0.20·min(disp.x,disp.y))`), a **resolution-scaled** value. The fix: size from content in **text-line units** + anchor to a shell edge. The same anti-pattern likely recurs across the shell — any panel whose extent derives from another element's resolution-scaled size, or that assumes the 1280x720 verify-capture resolution and can clip/overflow at the real runtime window (Ben runs 1920x1080; the window is resizable — see the `display-environment` memory + DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES § Display environment).

### Scope (audit + fix pass)
Walk each shell region (LAYOUT.md is the map) and check bounding at several resolutions / window sizes: **header** (top strip), **profile** (top-left), **nav rail**, **time panel** (top-right, sized off `mm_w`), **explorer**, **minimap** (+ its new lens bar), the **ledger windows** (shared `ledger_chrome` constants), and the **on-canvas lens keys / control strips**. For each: does it clip, overflow the screen, overlap a neighbour, or leave dead space when the window is small or large? Fix by sizing from content (`GetTextLineHeightWithSpacing()` / measured content) and anchoring to fixed shell edges, never to another element's resolution-scaled extent.

### Method
Drive the app at a few window sizes (e.g. 1280x720, 1920x1080, a small 1000x600) — the startup `Display:` log reports the runtime size — and capture each region. A `scripts/verify/*.lua` multi-resolution sweep would make this a repeatable check (candidate tool → skill). Proportional, Light-per-panel where a panel is already fine.

### Relationships
Generalises **BL-093**. Authority `docs/ui/LAYOUT.md` (+ each panel's own doc). Standing rule already in DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES § Display environment — this item is the application sweep, not a new rule.

items.title: UX review from the perspective of user stories — walk the player's goals end-to-end
items.summary: Idea (2026-07-04, Ben): review the whole UX from the perspective of USER STORIES rather than per-feature. Write the player's goals as stories ('as the player, I want to find where to grow and build there'; 'I want to know if a building is making money'; 'I want to read what a rival is doing'; 'I want to survey a new body and decide if it's worth it'; 'I want to see why I can't afford / can't build here') and walk each flow end-to-end through the actual UI, surfacing friction, dead ends, missing affordances, and ordering problems. Produces a prioritised list of UX fixes (many likely small, some feeding existing items like BL-082 panel occlusion). The Selection-element redesign (BL-093) is the model outcome — a surface reframed around what the player is trying to DO.
items.design:
**Status:** design-owed — captured 2026-07-04 (Ben). A review pass, not a feature.

### The idea
Evaluate the UX by **user story**, not by feature list. For each core player goal, write the story and walk it through the real UI, noting every point of friction. The Selection-element redesign (BL-093) came from exactly this lens ('what's my move here?') and is the template for the kind of reframe this produces.

### Candidate stories (starting set — expand at promotion)
- **Orient:** as the player, on load I want to know *who I am and where I am* (start framing / BL-085) and *what I could do next*.
- **Find opportunity:** I want to see *where to grow* at a glance without arming build mode (Opportunity/Industry lenses, BL-086).
- **Build:** I want to pick a tile, see *what I can build, what it costs (budget + materials), and why not* (BL-071/BL-044/BL-095), and do it in a few clicks.
- **Run my economy:** I want to know *if a building is profitable* and *whether I can afford things / my runway* (BL-074/BL-072/BL-073) without hunting across ledgers.
- **Expand:** I want to *survey a new body* and judge if it's worth the cost/ETA (BL-067).
- **Read the competition:** I want to *infer what rivals are doing* from public signals (BL-068/BL-089) — markets, activity, presence.
- **Trade:** I want to see *where my goods flow* and where demand is (BL-088/BL-089, market/scarcity lenses).

### Output
A prioritised list of concrete UX fixes/reframes — most likely small (labels, ordering, an affordance moved into reach, a dead-end given a next step), some feeding or superseding existing items (e.g. BL-082 construction-panel occlusion, BL-081 ledger legibility). File the findings as their own items or a batch; this item is the *review*, its children are the work.

### Method
Best run as an advisor+Ben session walking the live app story by story (the headless walkthrough + captures ground it), or a structured heuristic pass. Proportional — the deliverable is the ranked friction list, not a rewrite. Authority `docs/ui/LAYOUT.md` for any shell-level change; per-surface docs for the rest.

### Substrate (2026-07-05) — the artifact this review consumes now exists.
The user-story catalogue is built: `docs/development/user_stories.json` (canonical) + `USER_STORIES.md` (readable view). Legacy-feature pass (2026-07-05) covers 12 stories across all seven prototype clusters (orient/find/build/operate/expand/trade/read-rivals), every story requirement-linked to req/requirements.json brief slugs — so each is a walkable, testable acceptance path. This item is the REVIEW; the catalogue is the ARTIFACT. Run the walkthrough against the catalogue rather than re-deriving the story set; findings accrete onto each story's `friction` field. New/expanded stories are authored in `user_stories.json`, not here. See CLAUDE.md § Documents (user_stories) and § Source of truth (Player-intent coverage).

items.title: Commercial-fog proximity-glimpse peek — routing past a frontier body reveals it (deterministic)
items.summary: Deferred at BL-089's landing (recorded in its resolution): the deterministic proximity-glimpse 'peek'. When a player convoy completes a lane, sample body positions at that completion tick and mark any body within radius R of the lane segment as known_stale — a faint, decaying glimpse. Makes 'route past a frontier body to reveal it' discrete and deterministic (one sample at a discrete tick; positions are a pure function of tick — no per-frame test, no flicker, no RNG). R + freshness are headless-tuned calibration constants. BL-089 shipped the core fog (endpoint badge + corridor + Selection activity section) but this third illumination geometry was cut to land the item; captured here as its own promote-ready item. (Renumbered from BL-095 on merge to main 2026-07-05 — a cross-branch collision with main's BL-095 market-stockpile item.) DEFERRAL DECISION (v0.0.9 batch, 2026-07-05): assessed and HELD BACK. A faithful implementation needs either a serialised last_glimpse_tick on body_component (a save-seam change) or orbital back-computation from the mutated orbital_angle_rad — body position is NOT a pure function of tick today, contrary to the mechanic's premise, so 'sample body positions at the completion tick' cannot be reconstructed at a later render without stored state. Disproportionate determinism/serialisation risk for a polish minor; re-assess at the v0.1.0 boundary. Stays designed/promote-ready. [COMPLETE 2026-07-08 (BL-099 delivery): shipped via SAMPLE-AND-STORE, which dissolves the deferral objection. Positions ARE mutated (orbital_angle_rad, not pure in tick) as the deferral said -- so instead of reconstructing a past position, record_proximity_glimpses samples the closest-approach set ONCE at the discrete completion tick (credit_arrived_convoys, after orbits advanced for that frame, so live positions ARE the completion-tick positions) and stores the glimpse tick in world.body_last_glimpse_tick (off body_component, keeping the flat-binary layout untouched). body_activity_visibility returns known_stale for a glimpsed-but-unrouted body within glimpse_fresh_ticks_default (90), never known/visible; a body's own route outranks a glimpse; R=glimpse_radius_au_default (0.25 AU). The sample lives in supply_system.cpp (the actual completion hook -- the original files list omitted it); the renderer was NOT touched (the known_stale badge path is BL-089's, already blessed -- BL-099 only widens which bodies reach that tier). Verified: commercial_fog_harness 19/19 (10 new assertions -- geometry, tier, endpoint-exclusion, decay, route-precedence, determinism) + full CTest 19/19 (determinism intact); on-canvas by-eye via scripts/verify/proximity_glimpse.lua before/after. Authority propagated to DISCOVERY.md. Golden bless owed on the Linux box.]
items.design:
**Status:** designed — the design is settled inside BL-089's own note (§ 'Proximity glow (the peek)'); this item lifts that deferred slice out as a standalone, promote-ready unit. Requires BL-089 (shipped v0.0.8, commit af07ad0).

### What it adds (over the shipped fog)
BL-089 lit **endpoints** (bodies your routes actually reach) and **corridors** (the lit lane between them). This adds the **third illumination geometry**: a body you merely *pass near* on a completed lane gets a faint, decaying glimpse — the 'route past a frontier to reveal it' mechanic that makes commercial reach feel like expanding sight.

### Mechanic (deterministic — exactly as speced in BL-089)
- **Trigger:** when a player convoy **completes** a lane (a discrete tick), not per-frame.
- **Sample:** at that completion tick, compute body positions (a pure function of tick) and measure each body's closest approach to the endpoint→endpoint segment.
- **Mark:** any body whose closest approach ≤ radius `R` is set to **known_stale** — it enters the fog at the faint/greyed tier, never at `known`/`visible`. A glimpse, not a data feed.
- **Determinism:** one sample at a discrete tick, positions pure in tick ⇒ no per-frame proximity test, no orbital-drift flicker, no RNG. This is why BL-089 chose the discrete form over a live per-frame test.
- **State:** recomputable from routes + convoys + tick; if persisted it rides a `last_glimpse_tick` int on `body_component` (joins the save seam) — otherwise recomputed each read. No Lua, no per-tile exposure.

### Calibration
`R` (peek corridor half-width) and the freshness/decay window are **calibration constants**, headless-tuned. Start from the values BL-089's corridor rendering already uses; tune so a frontier body one 'hop' off a major lane glimpses while distant bodies do not.

### Files & seams
- `world.{hpp,cpp}` — the closest-approach sample at convoy completion; the `last_glimpse_tick` field if persisted. Reconcile with the existing `body_activity_visibility` derivation — the glimpse simply feeds the `known_stale` tier it already renders.
- `solar_system_canvas.cpp` — render the glimpsed body at the faint known_stale tier. The badge already exists from BL-089; this only widens which bodies reach it (plus, optionally, a soft mark along the corridor at the sample point).

### Requirement (Full mode)
- **`headless`** — extend `tools/verify/commercial_fog_*.cpp`: a frontier body within `R` of a completed player lane's segment returns `known_stale`; a body beyond `R` stays `unknown`; the glimpse set is a pure function of tick (same inputs → same set, no drift across recomputes).
- **`visual`** — extend `scripts/verify/commercial_fog.lua`: after a convoy completes a lane past a frontier body, that body shows the faint proximity glimpse. Golden-blessed.

### Authority
Lands into `docs/ui/DISCOVERY.md` (the activity-fog illumination geometry) — the peek completes the endpoint / corridor / proximity trio already described there.

items.title: Wire CTest + a one-command local build+test loop
items.resolution: Delivered. enable_testing() + a foreach over tools/verify/*.cpp builds every harness not already declared (world superset minus recipe_registry.cpp, mirroring CI) and registers add_test for all 14; the 7 hand-listed targets keep their minimal link sets; the 6 previously-unbuildable harnesses now build. check.bat = cmake --build + ctest. ctest -N = 14; econ_stability + world_audit verified building and passing. See req § ctest-wiring.
items.summary: 2026-07-05 sweep #4: no enable_testing()/add_test — `ctest` finds zero tests; 6 of 13 harnesses have no CMake target (only the CI bash glob builds them); no single build+test command exists locally, so a solo+AI loop that iterates many times a day re-assembles the check sequence by memory each time.
items.design:
**Status:** designed — settled from the 2026-07-05 health sweep (quick-win #4).

Add `enable_testing()` and replace the hand-listed harness targets with a **`foreach` over `tools/verify/*.cpp`** that (a) creates each harness `add_executable`, linking the same 'all `src/world/*.cpp` except `recipe_registry.cpp`' superset the CI loop uses (build.yml:83), and (b) registers `add_test(NAME <harness> COMMAND <harness>)`. Harnesses already exit non-zero on failure (CI relies on it), so they map to CTest for free. This fixes the 6 unbuilt targets, keeps CMake in lockstep with the CI glob (auto-picks up new harnesses incl. BL-106), and lets CI later replace its bespoke bash loop with `ctest`.

Add a thin **`check.bat`** (and mirror `check.sh` if wanted): `cmake --build build --config Release && ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure` — collapses the daily inner loop to one command.

**Caveat:** over-linking the world superset is safe because those TUs are SDL/Lua-free (recipe_registry excepted); it mirrors what CI already does. **Authority:** docs/development/DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md on landing.

items.design:
**Status:** designed — settled from the 2026-07-05 health sweep (quick-win #6).

New `tools/verify/determinism_harness.cpp` (modelled on corp_terrain_matrix's source set) that calls `make_hard_coded_world()` **twice** and asserts the two worlds are field-identical across the deterministic surface: body count + ids, per-body tile grid dimensions, per-tile terrain composition/landform and deposit arrays, tile→nation ownership, corporation placement/focus, building positions/types, market and population-centre placement.

items.title: Save-format magic + version header (reject mismatched saves on load)
items.summary: 2026-07-05 sweep #7 + completeness critic: the flat-binary save model is a load-bearing invariant that will evolve, but it is unversioned by design (a schema handshake is deferred to multiplayer per MULTIPLAYER_PRINCIPLES.md). The moment save/load lands and a struct layout changes between two dev builds, an old save silently misreads as UB garbage with no version guard to reject it.
items.design:
**Status:** designed but BLOCKED — settled from the 2026-07-05 health sweep (quick-win #7).

**Design:** reserve a fixed leading header on every flat-binary snapshot — a **magic uint32** (e.g. 'IOSV') plus a monotonically-incremented **format-version uint32** — written first and checked on load. A mismatched magic or version fails the load with a clear error rather than reading a struct-layout mismatch as garbage. Bump the version whenever a serialised struct's layout changes.

**BLOCKED:** no flat-binary serialiser exists in `world/*` yet (grep finds only PNG `fwrite` in `core/*`), so there is nothing to version. This item is the FIRST thing to add the moment serialisation is implemented.

**Shipped now under the 2026-07-05 batch:** the doc-truthfulness fix only — softening TECH_FOUNDATIONS' present-tense 'is serialised' / 'are written and read' claims to future tense so the invariant is not stated as already built.

**Note:** the serialisation implementation itself is not yet a backlog item — file one before promoting this.

**Shipped 2026-07-05 (health-sweep batch):** the doc-truthfulness half only — TECH_FOUNDATIONS § Save model / Serialisation softened from present tense ('is serialised' / 'are written and read') to future, with a forward-reference to this item's magic+version header. The item PROPER (the header) stays `designed` + blocked on the serialiser landing. **Authority:** docs/tech/TECH_FOUNDATIONS.md.

items.title: Unprotected sol2 .as<>() at startup can abort the process on a malformed data file
items.resolution: Delivered. main() wraps the run/run_verify dispatch in try/catch(const std::exception&), printing 'ProjectIo: fatal error: <what>' and returning 1 — a type-shape error in a user-edited economy.lua/recipes.lua (a sol::error, derived from std::exception) now exits cleanly instead of aborting unhandled, satisfying the standing 'no unprotected sol2' rule for all startup Lua paths. The optional per-key .as<>() guard in read_resource_map was judged unnecessary (the main() catch covers it) and left out to keep the change to one file. main.cpp compiles clean under /W4; ProjectIo.exe relinks. See req § sol2-startup-guard.
items.summary: 2026-07-05 sweep #10: read_resource_map converts Lua values with bare kv.first.as<std::string>() / kv.second.as<float>(); load_economy and main() have no try/catch, so a type-shape error in a user-edited economy.lua/recipes.lua throws sol::error and aborts with an unhandled exception. The standing rule forbids unprotected sol2 calls where errors can occur. Script LOADING is protected (safe_script_file); only type-shape errors within a well-formed script bite.
items.design:
**Status:** designed — settled from the 2026-07-05 health sweep (quick-win #10).

Smallest covering fix: wrap the app dispatch in `main()` (both `run_verify` and `run`) in **one `try/catch (const std::exception&)`** that prints the message to stderr and returns non-zero — this covers every startup Lua load path (load_economy → recipe_registry) at once, turning an unhandled-exception abort into a clean error exit.

**Optional hardening:** also guard the two `.as<>()` conversions in `read_resource_map` with the `sol::optional`/type-check pattern already used elsewhere in recipe_registry, for a precise per-key error message. Low severity — these are startup config files the solo dev controls, not a runtime hot path.

**Authority:** docs/tech/TECH_FOUNDATIONS.md (the sol2-safety invariant) / io-standing-rules.md.

items.title: Player opens at a net loss — verify build→produce→profit is reachable (or intended)
items.summary: Found 2026-07-06 in the playability audit: a fresh player opens running a NET LOSS (balance ledger showed inputs bought ~158/tick vs sales ~16/tick, net ~-166/qtr). Runway is long (~200yr) so it is not a hard blocker, but 'starts unprofitable with no obvious path to profit' is a viability question. Determine whether the starting corp can reach profit by building out its chain (and whether the player can tell how), or whether generation/pricing needs tuning. [DESIGNED 2026-07-07: intended pressure made legible — generation guarantees a fillable path, Opportunity lens surfaces unmet demand; headless fillability check.]
items.design:
**Status: DESIGNED 2026-07-07** (design session, Ben).

### Verdict: intended pressure, made legible (NOT a bug)
- Opening at a net loss is the intended early-game tension, PROVIDED the path to profit is fillable and visible.

### Two requirements at promotion
1. **Generation guarantees the path EXISTS** — the player's starting chain must be *capable* of reaching profit by filling an unmet demand gap (fillable), without pre-solving it.
2. **The Opportunity lens surfaces unmet population demand** — the gap the player should fill is legible on-canvas (ties US-003 / US-012).

### Verification
- Headless: instrument the player corp over N ticks (extend econ_harness / world_audit) under the new BL-078 demand model to confirm balance trends to profit after a sensible build-out — a *fillability check*, not a feature-vs-bug decision (settled: feature).

Couples to BL-078/BL-079 (economy dynamism) and BL-095 (materials). Authority → PRODUCTION.md on landing.

For each core interaction add a verify commit primitive (mirroring build_first_valid: mutate via the SAME code path the interactive control uses) + a verify.expect assertion + a scripts/verify/<flow>.lua acceptance script: recipe/workforce (set a building's recipe/target, tick, assert output changes), sell orders (place a standing order, clear, assert honoured over auto-sell), survey (dispatch, assert credits debited + reveal advances). items.title: Seeded world descriptor — New World setup (seed + resource abundance + nation count)
items.summary: A reproducible world descriptor — master seed + world_params (abundance tier, nation count, reserved body count) — chosen on a main-menu New World setup and threaded through make_hard_coded_world(world_params). Seed XOR-folds into each per-body seed literal (seed 0 reproduces the legacy world bit-for-bit); abundance is a pure post-multiply on deposits (sparse 0.40 / lean 0.65 / standard 1.00, the earth-like ceiling) that draws no RNG; nation count drives the Voronoi merge target. Descriptor lives in the app, off the serialisation seam. Verified headlessly by tools/verify/world_determinism.cpp (same seed→identical, different seed→different, sparse<lean<standard, default==legacy). Landed 2026-07-06 as a salvage-port onto main (originally authored off-main under the duplicated id BL-101; renumbered here — main's BL-101 is a different, closed item). body_count knob deferred to a follow-on (bodies are still hand-authored profiles).
items.design: **Status:** complete (landed 2026-07-06). The world descriptor is a small `world_params` struct — `seed` (uint32_t), `abundance` (sparse/lean/standard), `nation_count` (int), and a reserved `body_count` — plus a New World main-menu block that edits `m_pending_world_params` (seed hex entry + Roll/Copy, abundance radios, nation slider, a disabled bodies slider stub). `start_new_game()` consumes it; `setup_world(world_params)` records it in `m_active_world_params` and passes it to `make_hard_coded_world(world_params = {})`. Mapping: seed is XOR-folded into each existing per-body seed literal so seed 0 reproduces the legacy world exactly; abundance maps to a `deposit_scalar` applied as a pure post-multiply in `generate_body_tiles` Pass 6 (no RNG draw, so standard=1.0 is bit-identical to the unscaled surface, honouring the resource ceiling); nation_count sets `nation_params.merge_to` with `pre_seed_n = merge_to + 4` extra pre-merge seeds. The descriptor deliberately lives in the app, not the `world` struct, so it stays off the flat-binary save seam. Determinism/ordering verified by `tools/verify/world_determinism.cpp` (auto-registered as a CTest by the tools/verify/*.cpp glob). **Provenance:** salvage-ported from an off-main session that had duplicated much of v0.0.8/0.0.9 under divergent commits; this feature was its one genuinely-unique contribution. It was authored there citing 'BL-101', which collides with main's real (closed) BL-101 — renumbered to BL-114 throughout on landing. **Deferred:** the `body_count` knob (the body set is still the hand-authored Cinder/Kepler/Selene/Pallas profiles; a real count needs procedural body synthesis). Authority docs/generation/GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § The world descriptor.

items.title: Corporations open with a starting resource stockpile (prototype: fixed give)
items.resolution: Delivered (2026-07-06). corporation_generation.cpp seeds each corp's corp_body_pools[{corp, home_body}] with a fixed opening stockpile of the seven-resource prototype subset (iron ore 200; petroleum/water/agricultural 150; steel 100; refined fuel/food rations 80) via compute_starting_stockpile(); the home body is resolved from the corp's first placed asset (corp_home_body), and a corp with no holdings is skipped. Populates the existing corp_body_pools map — no new serialised field, no RNG, deterministic. Verified by the world_audit harness (BL-115 R1: 8/8 corps stocked with the exact give on their home body, 0 discrepancies, cold make_hard_coded_world). Immediately generalised by BL-116 (focus/wealth-shaped give replaces the flat constants). The credits-only material-cost workaround (a712b05) is deliberately untouched — re-enabling resource_costs is BL-095's scope (market-sourced), not this item.
items.summary: Idea (2026-07-06, Ben): players need to start with a stockpile of resources; for the prototype, *just give* a fixed one. Today corps open with capital but empty `corp_body_pools` (only the 12-tick pre-game warm-start puts any materials in), which is why the first building was made credits-only (a712b05, 'credits-only until BL-095'). Seed each corp's `corp_body_pools[{corp, home_body}]` with a fixed opening stockpile of the seven-resource prototype subset at generation time, symmetric across corps. Populates an existing serialised map (no save-format change, no RNG) so it stays deterministic. Superseded by BL-116 (generate it from focus/wealth); distinct from BL-095 (market stockpile); feeds BL-112 (opening viability).
items.design:
**Status:** designed — approach settled by Ben (2026-07-06): for the prototype, *just give* corporations a fixed opening resource stockpile. The exact resources/quantities are a tuning constant (settled at implementation, like other seeded/tuned economy values), not an open design question. Small, single-file, determinism-safe.

### The gap
Corporations open with **capital but no materials**. `corporation_generation.cpp` Pass 4 sets `starting_capital`/`balance` (`compute_capital`), but every corp's `corp_body_pools[{corp, body}]` opens empty — the only opening materials come from the 12-tick pre-game warm-start (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pre-game operating history). This left the very first building unbuildable from a cold pool; the construction deadlock was worked around by making the first building **credits-only** (commit a712b05, 'credits-only until BL-095'). A real opening stockpile removes the need for that workaround and lets build/production run from turn one.

### The prototype approach ('just give these')
At generation time — alongside the Pass 4 financial profile — seed each corporation's `corp_body_pools[{corp, home_body}]` with a **fixed opening stockpile** of the seven-resource prototype subset (RESOURCES.md: iron ore, petroleum, water, agricultural produce, steel, refined fuel, food rations). Symmetric across all corps (player included; the player is the actor in the prototype), so it composes with symmetrical rules and costs nothing extra. The stockpile is the seed the pre-game warm-start then evolves; the headless `--verify` cold path (no pre-game ticks) sees exactly the fixed give, so generation audits stay reproducible.

### Seam / determinism
- Populates the **existing** `corp_body_pools` map (`stockpile_component.quantities[r]`) — **no new serialised field**, no save-format change, no RNG. Fully deterministic.
- Set it next to `cc.starting_capital`/`cc.balance` in the corp assembly loop (`corporation_generation.cpp`, the Pass-4 corporation_component build). The corp's home body is the body its placed assets sit on.

### Requirement (at promotion)
Headless: after `make_hard_coded_world()` (cold, no pre-game ticks), every corporation's `corp_body_pools[{corp, home_body}]` holds the fixed opening quantities, and a first building is buildable from the corp pool without the credits-only workaround. Deterministic (same seed → same pools).

### Relationships
- **Superseded by BL-116** (generate the stockpile from focus + financial profile) — this fixed give is the prototype placeholder BL-116 replaces.
- **Feeds BL-112** (STARTING_ECONOMY_VIABILITY) — a real opening stockpile is part of whether the player opens at a reachable build→produce→profit position.
- **Distinct from BL-095** (markets hold a stockpile): this is the **corporation's** opening inventory (feeds its own production and what it can build/sell today); BL-095 later re-sources *build materials* to the **market**. When BL-095 lands, revisit whether markets also want an opening stock.
- Lets the **credits-only first-building** workaround (a712b05) be retired once the pool is reliably stocked.
- Authority docs/generation/CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pre-game operating history / Pass 4. Do not edit ahead of the work (authority time-slicing).

items.title: Generate the starting resource stockpile from corp focus + financial profile (replaces the fixed give)
items.resolution: Delivered (2026-07-06). Replaced BL-115's fixed compute_starting_stockpile() with generate_starting_stockpile(focus, capital, base_capital, rng) in corporation_generation.cpp. Model settled here: per-focus weights over the seven prototype resources (extraction hoards raws — iron 2.0, petroleum/water/agri 1.5, refined 0.3; processing pairs feed ~0.5-1.0 with refined output 0.8-1.2; trade carries finished goods 1.0-1.2 with thin raws 0.5), × a capital scalar (starting_capital / base_capital, clamped [0.5, 2.0]) so wealthier corps open deeper, × a seeded per-resource jitter [0.85, 1.15] drawn from an independent stream (seed_stock ^= 0xC3D4E5F6). Generated for every corp in a fixed draw order so the RNG stream stays deterministic even when a holdless corp is skipped; only corps with a resolvable home body receive a pool. No new serialised field. Verified by the world_audit harness (replacing BL-115's fixed-give assertion): R1 every corp opens non-empty + prototype-scoped (8/8) PASS; R2 focus correlation — extraction raw-stock mean 436.4 > trade 174.8 PASS; R3 determinism — 8 pools identical across two generations, 0 mismatched PASS. items.summary: Idea (2026-07-06, Ben): the second, proper item — generate the starting stockpile instead of the BL-115 fixed give. Derive each corp's opening `corp_body_pools` from its `industrial_focus` + financial profile (seeded, deterministic), so starting materials read as focus-coherent the way Pass-3 assets and Pass-4 capital already do — extraction opens rich in its raws, processing with feed+output, trade with products. items.design:
**Status:** design-owed — captured 2026-07-06 (Ben). The generative model that replaces BL-115's fixed give; model owed before promotion.

### The idea
The opening stockpile should be **generated**, not flat — derived from the corporation's `industrial_focus` and financial profile so a corp's starting materials read as coherent with who it is, the same way starting assets (Pass 3) and starting capital (Pass 4) already are. An extraction corp opens rich in the raws it mines; a processing corp opens with feedstock + some refined output; a trade corp opens with tradeable products and thinner raws. Seeded and deterministic, consistent with the rest of corporation generation.

### What exists today
After BL-115, every corp opens with a **fixed** `corp_body_pools[{corp, home_body}]` stockpile (identical for all). Capital already varies (`compute_capital`, `wealth_variance`); assets already follow focus (Pass 3). The opening stockpile is the one dimension still flat.

### Open design (owed)
- **Shape function.** Stockpile as a function of what? Candidates: `industrial_focus` (mix per focus, mirroring the Pass-3 asset mix), `starting_capital` (wealthier corps open deeper), home-nation resource profile, or a blend — which axes and their weights.
- **Per-focus resource mix.** Which resources each focus opens with (extraction → the raws it extracts; processing → feed + output; trade → products), grounded in the same focus→asset-mix patterns Pass 3 uses (and the open post-WW2 grounding item).
- **Magnitude / variance.** A seeded range + a variance knob (cf. `wealth_variance`), tunable in a headless harness; how many turns of runway the opening stock represents.
- **Player parity.** Symmetrical rules — the player generates on the same footing (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Player corporation); no special-case give.
- **Pre-game warm-start interaction.** The generated stock seeds the 12-tick warm-start; decide whether magnitudes assume the warm-start runs (GUI) or the cold `--verify` state.

### Seam / determinism
Same seam as BL-115 — populates the existing `corp_body_pools` map at generation time; **no new serialised field**. Draw from a seeded RNG (like `capital_rng` / `seed_capital`) so it stays deterministic and reproducible under `--verify`.

### Requirement (at promotion)
Headless: over a generated world, opening stockpiles correlate with focus (an extraction corp opens richer in its raws than a trade corp does) and with capital per the settled shape; deterministic (same seed → same pools). Replaces BL-115's fixed-give assertion.

### Relationships
- **Supersedes BL-115** (fixed prototype give) — generalises the flat opening stockpile into a focus/wealth-shaped one; land BL-115 first (cheap unblock), then replace its constants here. Not a hard `requires` (BL-116 could be built directly), but the intended sequence is prototype-first.
- **Feeds BL-112** (STARTING_ECONOMY_VIABILITY) — a focus-coherent opening stock is part of a reachable starting economy.
- Slots into corporation generation beside Pass 3 (asset mix) and Pass 4 (financial profile); shares their open **post-WW2 industrial grounding** item (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Open items).
- Distinct from BL-095/096 (market stockpiles / market generation) — this is the corp's opening inventory, not the market's.
- Touches generation only (no new save field) → determinism-sensitive, not a save-seam change. Do not edit CORPORATION_GENERATION.md ahead of the work (authority time-slicing).
- Authority docs/generation/CORPORATION_GENERATION.md.

### The principle (from the Construction-panel precedent)
A panel is a **bounded space for one class of question**; when it answers several unrelated questions it should expose a small nav (tabs or a button strip — construction_panel.cpp's redesign this session used a manual button-strip because ImGui::BeginTabBar's header mysteriously didn't render in this build/environment; worth retrying tabs once that's understood, but the button strip works and is the fallback) between separate bounded views, not one long scrolling stack.

Five `CollapsingHeader` sections in one window: **Corporation balances** (cross-corp comparison), **Stockpile pools** (corp x body inventory), **Workforce** (corp x body staffing), **Player balance trend** (a chart), **Markets** (supply/demand/price). These serve at least three different player questions: *how is everyone doing financially* (balances + trend), *what do I have and where* (stockpiles + workforce), *what's the market doing* (markets).

- **Grouping.** Which sections share a bounded view? A natural split: "Corporations" (balances + trend), "My Holdings" (stockpiles + workforce), "Markets" (supply/demand/price) — but confirm against how players actually use it.

Visual: each bounded view renders only its own question's content; the nav switches between them; no section answers more than one view's question.

items.resolution: Skeleton shipped (main session, 2026-07-06). New src/ui/foldout_column.{hpp,cpp} = the permanent left shell column: shell_column_width(disp.x)=clamp(round(0.17*x),300,360), foldout_column_rect(), foldout_begin/foldout_end (pinned borderless host). items.design:
**Status:** design-owed — captured 2026-07-06 (Ben, via Q&A during first live playtest of this session's build/economy/Construction-panel patches). Confirmed via Q&A: (1) "corporation identity tile" = the top-left profile_panel (emblem/name/parent/focus); (2) fold-out scope = ALL five ledger windows (Construction, Economy, Market Ledger, Balance Ledger, Corporations), not just Construction; (3) the identity tile / balance bar / selection element resize is PERMANENT — they stay at their new widths whether or not any menu is expanded (not a dynamic reflow only while something's open); (4) accordion behaviour — expanding one menu auto-collapses any other open one, only one fold-out panel is ever expanded at a time.

### The reframe
Today the shell is: a fixed-size profile box (top-left), a balance bar (top strip), a Selection element (bottom-left, pinned per SELECTION.md), a nav rail (icon buttons, left edge), and five independently-floating, freely-repositionable ImGui windows (Construction, Economy, Market Ledger, Balance Ledger, Corporations) that the player opens via the nav rail or window toggles. Ben wants a Paradox-style consolidated shell instead: the identity tile grows to ~1/6 screen width permanently (balance bar and Selection narrow to make room, permanently), and the five ledger windows stop floating — each becomes a tab that, when clicked, folds OUT to fill that same ~1/6-width column (not a separate floating window), and folds back IN to just its tab (not a collapsed thin bar) when toggled off or when another tab is opened.

### Confirmed decisions (from Q&A)
- Identity tile = profile_panel.cpp's existing corp emblem/name/parent/focus box.
- All five ledgers migrate to fold-out tabs: Construction, Economy, Market Ledger, Balance Ledger, Corporations. None stay as independent floating windows once this lands.
- Width changes (identity tile wider, balance bar + Selection narrower) are permanent/static, not conditional on any panel being open.
- Accordion, not stacking: opening a tab's fold-out collapses whichever other one was open. At most one fold-out panel expanded at a time.

### Open design (owed — settle before promotion)
- **Exact proportions.** Ben flagged "1/6" as approximate, not exact — needs a real number in px/fraction that works across the display-robustness constraint (DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES § Display environment: verify captures at 1280x720, Ben's runtime is 1920x1080 windowed-resizable; the column width should be content-sized or fraction-of-display, not a magic constant that clips at one resolution and floats at another).
- **Tab strip visual.** What the collapsed "menu tab" looks like and where it sits (a vertical strip of icon+label tabs down the edge, à la Paradox's side-menu icons? Under/beside the nav rail? Replacing the nav rail's existing icon buttons, or additive to them — nav_pane.cpp currently has its own icon rail whose relationship to this new tab strip needs deciding).
- **Relationship to the nav rail.** nav_pane.cpp already provides icon-button navigation; clarify whether the new fold-out tab strip absorbs nav_pane's role (one rail, not two) or sits alongside it as a second, distinct affordance.
- **Content re-hosting.** Each ledger's current window body (draw_economy_panel, draw_market_ledger, draw_balance_ledger, draw_corporation_panel, draw_construction_panel) needs to render inside a fixed-width fold-out column instead of a freely-sized ImGui::Begin window — check each for hardcoded/assumed widths that won't survive being squeezed into ~1/6 screen (economy_panel's tables especially; BL-117's split should probably land in this same column-width layout rather than its own floating window, so sequence BL-117..121 against this item).
- **Animation vs instant.** Does fold in/out animate (slide) or snap instantly? A snap is far cheaper and more prototype-appropriate; note it either way.
- **Selection element interaction.** Selection is pinned bottom-left per SELECTION.md and BL-093 sized it from content, not a resolution-scaled dimension — its permanent narrowing here needs to compose with that existing content-sizing fix, not fight it.
- **Tab bar rendering caveat.** This session's Construction-panel redesign found `ImGui::BeginTabBar`'s header didn't render visibly in this build/environment for unknown reasons (worked around with a manual button strip) — investigate that before assuming a native ImGui tab-bar widget is available for the tab strip here; may need the same button-strip fallback.

### Sequencing with BL-117..121
Those five items settle each panel's *internal* one-question-per-view split (e.g. Economy panel's 5 sections → bounded sub-views). This item is the *outer shell* — the fold-out column that hosts whichever view each of those items settles on. Natural order: settle BL-117 (Economy, the most tangled) enough to know its view count, then build this shell so each ledger's settled views become sub-tabs or sections within its fold-out. Not a hard blocking dependency (this item's shell can be built with each panel's current content first, and the BL-117..121 splits layered in after), but doing them together avoids rework.

### Requirement (at promotion)
Visual: at 1280x720 and 1920x1080, the identity tile/balance bar/Selection show their new permanent widths; each of the five tabs folds its own content out to the shared column and back to just its tab (not a floating window, not a thin collapsed bar); opening a second tab collapses the first; no clipping/overlap at either resolution (ties into BL-097's resolution-robustness sweep).

### Relationships
Supersedes the floating-window model BL-117..121 assumed; hosts their eventual per-panel splits. Shares the resolution-robustness concern with **BL-097** (view bounding audit) and the content-sizing precedent from **BL-093** (Selection element). Authority `docs/ui/LAYOUT.md` — do not edit ahead of the work (authority time-slicing).

### Settled (2026-07-06 design session — decisions locked, status → designed)
Scope confirmed as the **shell skeleton only** (Ben): build the fold-out column + re-host the five named ledgers + permanent width changes + verify; the per-panel one-question splits (BL-117..121) and the Tile Ledger's migration are reassessed *after*, not inside this item.
- **Column anatomy — rail left, panel right.** The existing 56px icon rail (nav_pane) stays permanently visible at the far-left edge; each live slot folds its panel OUT into the `[56, W]` space to its right. The rail IS the tab strip — one rail, not two. Canvas shows through the `[56, W]` body when nothing is expanded.
- **Column width `W` = `clamp(round(0.17 × disp.x), 300, 360)` px**, computed at runtime from `ImGui::GetIO().DisplaySize` (~300 @1280, ~326 @1920). Replaces the compile-time `profile_panel_width = 200`; runtime-from-display IS the display-robustness fix. The 300px floor is deliberate — it forces the BL-117..121 splits rather than leaving them optional.
- **Identity tile** (profile_panel) widens to `W`, top-left, permanent. Emblem/name content unchanged for the skeleton.
- **Balance bar & Selection narrow permanently** — both move their left origin to `x = W` (header's `header_left`, selection's `left_x`; already parameterised, ~one line each). Selection's BL-093 content-height sizing is untouched — only its left edge moves.
- **Five named ledgers migrate** (Construction, Economy, Market, Balance, Corporations): each loses its floating `ImGui::Begin` and draws into the shared fold-out column at the column geometry. Current bodies hosted as-is (economy tables get horizontal scroll until BL-117).
- **Construction's BL-082 special anchor dissolves** — the column ends above Selection by construction, so Construction becomes an ordinary fold-out tab.
- **Tile Ledger / History (slot 9) stays floating for now** — nav menu items unchanged; only the five named ledgers fold out in this item. Its migration is a later call.
- **Accordion reused as-is** — nav_pane's `close_all_panels` already enforces one-open-at-a-time; no new state.
- **Tab widget: manual Selectable strip**, reusing construction_panel's `nav_button` pattern — `BeginTabBar` confirmed non-rendering in this build/environment.
- **Fold in/out is an instant snap** — no slide animation, no animation state.
- **Content re-host behind a shared `draw_foldout_column`** (new) that positions one borderless window at the column rect and dispatches to the active panel's body; app stops positioning five separate windows.
