items.title: Prose-analysis pass on the central documentation
items.summary: Idea (2026-07-07, Ben, end of the ledger-mockup session): a prose-analysis pass on the CENTRAL documentation — CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/io-standing-rules.md, DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md, DELIVERY.md. Prompted by the observation that these docs specify the discipline of development entirely in the negative (what to avoid, 'favour X over Y', 'no ceremony') and never name the reward — the craft / enjoyment of the work. The prose is Ben's to write; this item just captures the analysis + candidate framings for when he is in the mood. Not urgent (Ben: 'won't change it soon') but rated SSS: the central docs are the project's operating system, so their prose quality is strategically load-bearing. [COMPLETE 2026-07-08: Ben explicitly delegated the prose ('rewrite the docs'); 18 clause-level edits landed across the four docs — reward named around every rule, no rule text changed.]
items.design:
**Seed observation.** The central docs name the *constraints* of good development well but never the *satisfactions* — they say what to avoid, rarely what to reach for or savour. A prose pass could name the reward without tipping into motivational-poster register.

**Candidate framings (from the 2026-07-07 discussion — Ben picks; the prose is his):**
- *Legibility as a pleasure, not just a constraint* — 'favour legible over clever' is defensive; name the payoff instead: a good solution reads as obvious in hindsight and is a pleasure to explain.
- *The proportionate as its own reward (Rule 0)* — a clean one-liner is a genuine pleasure; don't rob a small win of it with ceremony. Rule 0 frames Light as the cheap option; it is often the satisfying one.
- *Flow* — the docs are all gates and barriers; nothing blesses momentum. Something like 'when the path is clear, keep moving; save the ceremony for the seam.'
- *The click / the quietly-wrong* — name the satisfaction of finding the thing that is secretly wrong (the fix that also dissolves a latent problem; e.g. the lens-key reposition that pre-empted a future overlap).
- *Taste as a valid input* — when something reads wrong, fixing it is work, not vanity (the '||' → square pause glyph).
- *The loop mirrors the game* (the strongest, Io-specific one) — Project Io prizes legible, composable systems that justify themselves by feeding Trade or Conflict; describe the development process in the same words: each change feeds something, composes cleanly, reads legibly. A game about elegant systems, built by an elegant system.
- *The word 'fun' itself* may land light in that register; heavier synonyms carry the same energy — craft, satisfaction, momentum, or (for a game) play.

**Scope.** Analysis + rewording of the Tone / Rule-0 / working-method sections primarily. Doc-only, no code. Authority: the docs themselves.

**Delivered 2026-07-08.** Ben's 'rewrite the docs' overrode the prose-is-Ben's reservation. Method: survey (4 per-doc + 1 voice-anchor agents) → three competing full drafts (minimal-weave / one-named-home / full-coverage) → three-lens judge panel (register skeptic / operating-system critic / craft judge) → main-session synthesis → three-skeptic adversarial verify over the applied diff. Landings: framing 6 anchored as a three-sentence passage in DELIVERY.md § The one idea with a one-sentence echo in CLAUDE.md's pipeline intro (two appearances, no more); framing 2 as the 'small win stays whole' kernel in CLAUDE.md's Light bullet, full form ('a clean one-liner is a pleasure') in DELIVERY; framing 5 one home (DELIVERY § Ad-hoc ideas, scoped to Rule 0a's two-option offer); framing 4 at the two verification seams ('the quietly-wrong'); framing 1 as the Tone-pair gradient (standing-rules terse 'the clever one is a debt', DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES fuller 'a pleasure to explain'); framing 3 in the thesis ('the ceremony is for the work that earns it') + pausing ('resumes without archaeology'). Deliberately omitted: 'a game about elegant systems, built by an elegant system' (poster-register risk — Ben may add); the standing-rules preamble and Development-constraints intro left untouched (panel consensus: highest standing cost / factually-wrong rationale). A post-apply adversarial verify (rule-preservation / register / echo-integrity skeptics; 11 findings) drove 8 corrections — notably rescoping the taste sentence under Rule 0a (as placed in the Light bullet it licensed unscoped drive-by fixes), broadening 'the ceremony is for the seam' to 'the work that earns it' (it mis-narrowed Full's three triggers), keeping the standing rules ornament-free, and disambiguating DP's preamble addition to 'the note rides along' (the original silently upgraded 'suggest' to 'apply inline'). Accepted-as-is over verifier objection: the pleasure/kernel sentences (they ARE the item's payload), the shared 'quietly-wrong' coinage, generic 'debt' (canonical term 'explanation debt' unused).

items.design: Post-optimization revisit of the BL-095 stock model. Decide whether markets should hold a **real persistent per-resource inventory** (fills from production + nation capacity, drains to consumption + construction) rather than a derived-from-recent-supply figure. Trade-off: a real inventory is the cleanest substrate for "greedy actors compete for stock" and for runtime market split/merge (BL-132), but adds a serialized array to the flat-binary seam and deterministic tick accounting. Gate: only worth doing after a general optimization/efficiency pass. `requires` BL-095. Authority → PRODUCTION.md on landing.

items.title: Full market/population co-generation — population near resources, markets on trade routes, corp carving
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-07 from the economy design session. BL-096's first cut keeps population placement as-is and carves markets by nation territory. Ben's fuller ideal: population spawns near rich resources, and markets are centred on rich trade routes, with corps (not just nations) carving resource clusters. Settled 2026-07-21 (Sprint 1 procgen review): BL-096 (its blocker) has since shipped and the three-change sequencing is now fixed — promote-ready.
items.design:
The fuller co-generation vision deferred from BL-096. Three coupled changes: (1) **population spawns near rich resources** — make generate_population_centres resource-aware; (2) **markets centred on rich trade-route proxies** — since live routes do not exist at gen-time, derive a static resource↔population trade-flow proxy and centre markets on it; (3) **corp-level carving** — place corps before markets (a generation reorder) so competing corporations, not just nations, carve resource clusters. Larger rewrite touching hard_coded_world / nation_generation / market seeding; determinism-sensitive. `requires` BL-096. Authority → GENERATION_STRATEGY.md on landing.

### Settled 2026-07-21 (Sprint 1 procgen review)
**Blocker cleared.** BL-096 (resource-driven market generation) has since shipped — this item's stated dependency is satisfied.

**Sequencing fixed: (1) → (2) → (3), in that order — no reorder.** Population-resource-awareness lands first (a self-contained change to `generate_population_centres`, no reorder of the wider pipeline). The trade-flow proxy lands second, since it reads the now-resource-aware population placement. Corp-level carving lands last, since it's the one genuine generation **reorder** (corps before markets) and should not be entangled with the other two while they're still landing.

**Layer relationship to this sprint's sibling-pass decision (BL-051).** This item operates one layer above tile generation — it's world-seeding order (population → markets → corps), not a tile-generation pass — so the sibling-pass convention doesn't directly apply here; no conflict, just a different extension point. Flipped `design-owed` → `designed`: scope was already well-specified, the blocker is cleared, and sequencing is now fixed.

items.title: Opportunity lens reads uniformly green — differentiate unmet demand + drop the qualifier
items.summary: Found 2026-07-08 in the lens-legibility review (Ben). The Opportunity lens shows all-green — it is not differentiating actual unmet demand. Root cause: the metric is each market's biggest ABSOLUTE price/base_price ratio (body_surface_canvas.cpp ~698); in a saturated economy where every market bids above its floor, every catchment reads as opportunity, so it is uniform. Also drop the '(unmet demand)' qualifier from the lens name/legend (overlay.cpp:75, body_surface_canvas.cpp:160) — Ben: it just confuses. The label drop is trivial; the metric differentiation is the substance.
items.design: Two parts, both now settled. (1) **Label (trivial):** drop the '(unmet demand)' qualifier — overlay_mode_name returns 'Opportunity' (overlay.cpp:75), the legend title becomes 'Opportunity' (body_surface_canvas ~160), and the widened (~190px) key box shrinks back to the standard width. (2) **Metric (settled — Ben):** replace the current max-absolute price/base ratio per market (which saturates green because every market in the saturated economy bids over its floor) with a **body-relative, volume-weighted rank of the unmet-demand gap**. For each catchment/market on the body: compute its demand gap, weight it by demand volume (so a large market's gap outranks a tiny market's high-ratio blip), then rank/normalize across the body's markets so the strongest gaps read green and met markets read neutral→red. Mirrors the Scarcity lens's body-relative treatment. Feeds the red→green mark of VALUE_LENS_TILE_MARKS (BL-135). Authority → LENSES.md on landing. 2026-07-08 lens-legibility batch.

items.title: Tile selection opens a tile-detail ledger that includes its building (one tile = one building)
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-08 (Ben). Selecting a tile should open a ledger/view that LEADS with tile detail (what the tile is — terrain, deposits, owner) and also surfaces the ONE building on it, with a way to navigate (double-click) into that building's own detail. Confirms the existing one-building-per-tile invariant (placement_reason::occupied already blocks a second building per tile). Currently tile and building are separate selection_kinds (selection_panel.cpp) — tile selection shows tile detail + a build front-door, building selection shows building detail — so the two are not unified as tile-primary-with-building.
items.design:
**Settled (interaction; layout split is a Ben mockup input).** Make the TILE the primary selection subject. Selecting a tile opens the tile ledger whose lead content answers 'what is this tile' — terrain composition/landform, deposits, territory owner, habitability. If a building occupies the tile it appears as a sub-element; double-click navigates into the building's full detail (the existing single-click-selects / double-click-navigates model, SELECTION.md).

**Build front-door (Ben, settled):** the empty-tile 'place a building' affordance is NOT folded inline and is NOT a separate ledger state — instead the tile ledger carries, **near its top, a navigation affordance to a specialised build ledger**. Building is reached by navigating from the tile, keeping the tile ledger tile-primary and the build flow its own specialised surface. Couples to BL-143, which removes the Building ledger's build front-door so that building is only ever reached via a tile.

**Invariant (confirmed, already enforced):** each tile carries at most ONE building (placement_reason::occupied rejects a second), so 'the building on this tile' is always 0 or 1 — which is what makes the tile-primary framing clean.

**Future (noted, NOT this item):** a building may gain LEVELS or change its resource/production path over its life; the tile-ledger layout should leave room without designing it now.

items.title: Containerise every text/image — wrap or fit, never truncate in narrow views
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-08 (Ben). Text is being truncated/clipped in narrow views. Ben: every image or line of text must be containerised so it either WRAPS or is guaranteed to FIT its defined space — never silently truncated. Scope (measured 2026-07-08): ~255 ImGui text calls across 17 UI files with ZERO use of TextWrapped/PushTextWrapPos (nothing wraps today), plus 37 draw-list AddText labels across 5 canvas files (painted legends/labels that overflow their boxes — cf. the market-legend key auto-size fix). Requires the container spec (BL-141) first.
items.design:
**Settled — mechanical application of the BL-141 container vocabulary; requires BL-141.** Systemic pass: every on-screen text/image is placed in a BL-141 container and takes that container's text policy — **wrap** (PushTextWrapPos/TextWrapped) or **guaranteed-fit** (CalcTextSize → size, the market-legend key pattern). No silent truncation at supported widths (down to the 1280×720 verify window and the narrower fold-out columns). Images/markers clamped to container (max-fit).

Current state (measured 2026-07-08): ~255 ImGui text calls across 17 files, none wrapping; 37 draw-list AddText across 5 canvas files. **Decomposes per-surface at promotion** — header/balance strip, time panel, on-canvas legends, selection element, ledgers, hover card, ImGui tables. Each surface takes its container's policy from BL-141, applies wrap-or-fit, and is verified at the narrow width. Broad but mechanical. Relates to BL-063. Authority → LAYOUT.md on landing. 2026-07-08 UX review.

items.title: Define each permitted UI container (the container vocabulary)
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-08 (Ben). Foundation for BL-140: before we can containerise every text/image, we must enumerate the ALLOWED containers — the fixed set of layout boxes the UI is built from (fold-out ledger column, on-canvas legend box, selection element, header/balance strip, time panel, hover card, minimap lens bar, nav rail, ImGui tables) — each with its sizing rule (fixed / stretch / fit-to-content) and its text policy (wrap vs fit). Every piece of on-screen text/image must then live inside one of these. Lands in LAYOUT.md as the container spec.
items.design:
**Settled — the closed container vocabulary (draft below for Ben's blessing; exact px are his at landing).** The UI is built from a fixed set of containers; every on-screen text/image must live in exactly one. Each is specified by sizing, min/max, text policy, and overflow. Two text policies only: **wrap** (PushTextWrapPos/TextWrapped) or **guaranteed-fit** (measure with CalcTextSize → size the box, the pattern the market-legend key now uses). Images/markers clamp to their container (max-fit).

1. **Fold-out ledger column** (foldout_column) — fixed-width, stretch-to-height, docked to the canvas edge; text **wrap** to inner width; overflow → vertical scroll.
2. **On-canvas lens legend box** (draw-list, body_surface_canvas) — **fit-to-content** (measure → size); text **guaranteed-fit**; no overflow (box grows to fit).
3. **Selection element** (selection_panel) — fixed-width panel (resize pass = BL-123); text **wrap**; overflow → vertical scroll.
4. **Header / balance strip** (header_panel) — stretch-to-width, fixed height; text **guaranteed-fit** (measured segments, never wraps to a second line); overflow → elide-with-tooltip only as a last resort, never silent truncation.
5. **Time panel** (app.cpp) — fixed; text **guaranteed-fit** (authored to fit); no overflow.
6. **Hover card** — fit-to-content with a max width; text **wrap** at max width; overflow → grow vertically.
7. **Minimap lens bar** — fixed strip; icon-only / guaranteed-fit labels; no overflow.
8. **Nav rail** — fixed; icon-only, tooltips wrap.
9. **ImGui table** (ledgers) — stretch columns with min widths; per-cell **guaranteed-fit** (clip + tooltip) or **wrap** for description columns; overflow → horizontal scroll on the table, never silent truncation of load-bearing values.

This lands as a LAYOUT.md section (the authority) and **gates BL-140**, which applies it everywhere. Open (Ben, at landing): confirm the list is complete and set the exact min/max px per container. 2026-07-08 UX review.

items.title: Generated road network + A* cost integration
items.completion_note: Landed 2026-07-10. New src/world/road_generation.{hpp,cpp}: generate_roads(w, body) runs in hard_coded_world.cpp after generate_nations, deterministically stamping tile.road_level. Per nation over its population centres: pairwise terrain-weighted A* (intra_body_path) costs, Kruskal MST tie-broken by (cost, lo-tile-id, hi-tile-id), plus relative-neighbour redundancy edges; trunk (road_level 2) between major centres (scale>=3) else local (1); rasterised along the A* path taking max road_level and skipping ocean. Then one local border link between the nearest centre pair of each territorially-adjacent nation pair (4-cardinal + column-wrap adjacency scan). Clears world.astar_cost_cache at the end (roads were measured road-free for the MST, so the cache is stale after stamping) per the world.hpp invalidation contract. Tuning settled with Ben: local=1/trunk=2, major=scale>=3. Verified headless via tools/verify/road_generation_harness.cpp: R1 lattice exists + no ocean roads, R2 both tiers present + none exceed trunk, R3 14/14 non-isolated centres touch a road, R4 road_level identical across two generations (determinism). Regression: determinism/logistics/trade_routes/econ/world_audit harnesses all green. Authority propagated to SUPPLY.md + TILE_GENERATION.md. Rendering + player placement follow in BL-147; no on-canvas surface yet.
items.summary: Follow-on from BL-077 (core), split out 2026-07-08. The world ships pre-roaded: a deterministic per-nation generation pass lays a realistic road lattice over nation territory (stamping road_level onto tiles), and road_level lowers A* traversal cost so routing prefers roads. The nation lattice + cities-as-hubs (BL-148) give the player a low-cost network to plug into; player road-building (BL-147) then reaches out to remote extraction sites.
items.design:
Follow-on from BL-077 (core). Requires the core's road_level field, per-body grid index, and terrain-weighted A* pathfinder. Runs AFTER nation + population generation (it needs cities to connect) — slots into hard_coded_world.cpp after generate_nations (~line 158).

**Road-generation pass (deterministic from the campaign seed).** Per nation:
1. **Nodes** = the nation's population centres.
2. **Weighted graph** = terrain-weighted A* path cost between each centre-pair (one-off at generation; small node count, not per-Tick).
3. **Backbone = MST + redundancy** — minimum spanning tree over that graph, then a few short extra edges (relative-neighbour rule: keep an edge unless a third centre is closer to both endpoints) for realistic loops. Deterministic tie-break: sort candidate edges by (cost, lower-node-id, higher-node-id).
4. **Two-tier hierarchy** — edges among major centres (City/Metropolis) become **trunk** roads (higher road_level, larger cost cut); spurs linking smaller settlements to their nearest backbone node become **local** roads.
5. **Rasterise** each edge as its terrain-weighted A* path; stamp road_level on the crossed tiles (max on overlap); paths respect the east-west cylinder wrap.
6. **Border links** — after the per-nation networks exist, add one link between the nearest city-pair across each adjacent-nation boundary, so the continent-wide lattice is connected.

Cities enumerable via world.population_centres + population_centre_tile. New TU road_generation.{hpp,cpp} keeps the pass off the tile_generation hotspot; wired in hard_coded_world.cpp (main-session integration). Determinism guard: add road_level to the determinism_harness field checks.

**Tuning (settle at promotion):** trunk/local road_level values and their A* cost-cut. **Authority:** SUPPLY.md (road cost-reducer) + TILE_GENERATION.md (the generation pass).

items.title: Render the commercial-activity fog as a dim shadow (make the unlit map read as fogged)
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-08 (Ben) after observing the commercial-activity fog reads as 'no fog'. Today (BL-089) the activity fog is ABSENCE-by-default: an unknown body draws nothing (a plain astronomy dot); only known/known_stale/visible non-home bodies get a small ~4-6px lower-left pulse badge. So with no player commerce the whole Solar map looks identical to no-fog, and even when lit the badges are subtle next to the survey '?' + labels. This item inverts the treatment: render the fog as a DIM SHADOW over bodies outside the player's commercial network, so the unlit map READS as fogged and brightens as commerce reaches it.
items.design:
**Problem.** The commercial-activity fog (BL-089, `body_activity_visibility` -> Solar badges in `solar_system_canvas.cpp:249`) is a presence-badge on LIT bodies, not an overlay on the dark. Unknown bodies draw nothing, so the fog is invisible until the player runs commerce, and the small lower-left pulse dots are easily lost. Prompted by Ben 2026-07-08 ('I'm not seeing any fog').

**Change.** Render the activity fog as a **dim shadow**: bodies the player's commercial network does NOT reach are drawn dimmed/shadowed on the Solar canvas (a translucent dark wash and/or reduced body+label brightness), so the un-networked map legibly reads as *fogged*; as a route/convoy reaches a body it **brightens** to full (known -> visible a rising brightness ramp). The existing lower-left pulse badge can stay as the fine-grained tier tell for the lit tiers; the shadow is the new coarse read for the unlit. Keep it visually distinct from the geographic **survey** fog (BL-067, the '?' badges) — the two fogs must still read apart (DISCOVERY.md's two-independent-fogs rule).

**Scope.** Solar canvas only (the activity fog is body-level). Home stays full-bright (its BL-085 halo). Derived read only — no new sim state (reads `body_activity_visibility`). `presentation.hpp/.cpp` for the shadow colour/alpha + brightness ramp; `solar_system_canvas.cpp` for the per-body dim.

**Landed 2026-07-09.** Per-body dimming (chosen over regional wash); brightness ramp unknown/stale/known/visible = 0.36/0.60/0.84/1.0 with shadow-wash alpha 105/50/0/0; known_stale reads partially-lit. `dim_rgb` helper + `activity_fog_*` ramps in presentation.hpp; per-body dim in solar_system_canvas.cpp. **Authority:** docs/ui/DISCOVERY.md (activity-fog rendering).

items.title: Intra-body commercial-reach fog on the Planetary canvas (surface reads as mostly unknown)
items.summary: Filed + landed 2026-07-09 (Ben, follow-on from BL-150). The commercial-activity fog (BL-089) is body-level only, rendered on the Solar canvas; the Planetary canvas had no activity fog, so the home surface read as fully known. Ben expected fog of war on the home planet over intra-body trade. This adds a THIRD visibility treatment: a per-tile intra-body fog on the Planetary canvas so the surface reads as mostly unknown, lit only around the player's own presence.
items.design:
**Semantics (Ben's call).** Commercial reach, not unknown-terrain: the home planet is the player's own territory, so 'fog' means *where your logistics actually operate*. **Substrate (Ben's call).** Live-derived, no stored state / no save-format change; intra-body traffic records nothing persistent.

**Model.** Vision is a TIGHT pocket around the player's actual presence, not a whole market catchment (a first cut lit the entire catchment — Ben: 'too wide'; the point is a sense of movement + unknowns). Reveal sources: the player's own building tiles + the endpoint (`centre_tile`) of any live player convoy on the active body. A breadth-first flood out to `fog_reveal_radius` (=3) tile-hops from every source marks the visible pocket (odd-r offset neighbours, column wrap); every other revealed tile takes a dark wash (`lerp 0.5` toward IM_COL32(8,10,16)). Applied over the lens fill (a fogged region's analytic read dims with it). The geographic survey fog (BL-067) still owns unrevealed tiles — this dims revealed ones only. Always-on, all overlays. Convoys confirmed live (dispatch/advance/credit run every econ step, app.cpp:381).

**Verify.** `scripts/verify/intrabody_fog.lua` (goto_surface home + zoom-out capture). Probe at landing: home body 7 markets, player reaches 1 -> 6 catchments fogged; tightened to radius pockets so the HQ region reads lit and the rest of the globe fogged at both play and wide zoom.

**Follow-up -> BL-152:** a live convoy should emit a radius-2 vision BEAM that travels its route and lags/dims over ~1 econ tick (needs `logistics_path` to return its tile sequence — currently cost-only). That is the 'things are moving' half; this item is the static-presence half.

items.title: Convoy vision beam — a live convoy lights a radius-2 beam that lags and dims over one econ tick
items.summary: Filed + landed 2026-07-09 (Ben, the 'things are moving' half of BL-151). A live player convoy emits a radius-2 beam of vision along the tiles it moves through; that vision lags and dims over one econ tick (90 days). The moving-presence complement to BL-151's static-presence pocket.
items.design:
**Spec (Ben).** 'Convoys should send a radius 2 beam of vision which lags and dims over 1 econ tick.'

**Path exposure.** `logistics_path` (world.hpp) gained a `tiles` sequence; `intra_body_path` (logistics.cpp) reconstructs it via a came_from parent-walk, stored in canonical lo->hi endpoint order (the route cache is keyed on the unordered pair). Deterministic; wrap-aware (the grid is a horizontal cylinder). Verified by a throwaway headless probe (contiguity, canonical order, single-tile src==dst).

**Vision buffer.** `ui_state.convoy_vision` maps tile -> the sim time (elapsed days) a beam last lit it; `ui_state.sim_now_days` is the continuous fade clock (set every frame in app.cpp). Derived VIEW state only — never serialised, no feedback into world/*, so world determinism is preserved (a `world/*` standing rule).

**Refresh (per econ step).** `ui::update_convoy_vision` (body_surface_canvas) runs in app::step_economy after advance_convoys (before arrived convoys are retired). For each live player intra-body convoy it maps progress -> a path-index segment (where it was one tick ago .. now), floods radius-2 (odd-r neighbours) around that segment, and stamps now_days. Prunes entries older than one econ tick.

**Render.** The Planetary fog (BL-151) now blends a beam vision term: vision = 1 in the static pocket, else max with the beam's fading contribution (1 - age/90); fog wash = 0.5*(1 - vision). So a convoy's beam trails and dims behind it over one econ tick. Uses continuous sim time, so it fades smoothly between quarter boundaries rather than snapping.

**Scope note.** Intra-body convoys only (inter-body activity reads on the Solar fog, BL-089/150). econ_tick_days (90) mirrored as a local constant in the canvas to avoid a ui->core include. **Authority:** docs/ui/DISCOVERY.md.

**Superseded 2026-07-09 by BL-154:** the per-econ-step segment-flood + timestamp-fade was replaced by a render-time moving head/tail beam (interpolated by econ-tick fraction) + permanent corp-centre->market corridors. The path-exposure work here stands; the buffer/refresh mechanism was reworked.

items.title: Convoy payout weighted by haul distance, not just destination price
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-09 (Ben, alongside the convoy vision work). Ben: players should 'get money based on distance rather than just time'. Today a convoy has NO time- or distance-based payout: its cargo is delivered into the destination market and sold at the live clearing price (the price differential IS the profit); logistics COST already scales with path distance (logistics_cost x A* path cost). So distance shows up as a cost, not a revenue term. This item asks whether long hauls should also PAY more — a distance-scaled delivery margin on top of the price differential.
items.design:
**Settled 2026-07-26 (AI design session; drafted by Claude, ratified by Ben same day).** Distance becomes a revenue lever via a **zero-sum freight premium** - option (c) grounded, chosen over (a) a minted distance bonus (dishonest money - conflicts with the honest-constraints principle) and over (b) legibility-only (Ben explicitly wants distance-based pay).

**Mechanism.** When convoyed cargo sells at the destination, the hauler is credited a **freight premium per unit**: `premium = k_freight x haul_distance x unit_price`, funded by a matching uplift on the destination market's effective buy price for that clearing pass - buyers pay the freight, the hauler earns it, no money is minted. Long-haul supply into an undersupplied market is genuinely better-paid; gluts still crash the price (the premium scales with the cleared price, so a worthless delivery earns a worthless premium).

**Seams.** credit_arrived_convoys (supply_system.cpp) records haul distance on the convoy at dispatch (intra_body_path cost or inter-body transfer distance, per mode); clear_markets (market_clearing.cpp) applies the premium at settlement so it composes with the order book. Deterministic; touches the economy seam -> Full mode, verifier-headless check on the zero-sum invariant (sum of premiums == sum of buyer uplift, exactly).

**AI relevance (why now).** The BL-202 route scorer needs a definite payout formula: `net = qty x (dest_price - src_price) + premium(distance) - logistics_cost(distance, mode)`. This settles it.

**Tuning note.** k_freight starts small (premium < logistics cost on short hauls, > on long ones) - the lever makes distance pay, not print. Constant lives in economy.lua with the logistics costs. **Authority** -> docs/economy/SUPPLY.md (not PRODUCTION.md - freight is a logistics-revenue rule) on landing.

items.title: Moving head/tail convoy beam + permanent corp-centre-to-market corridors
items.summary: Filed + landed 2026-07-09 (Ben, refining BL-151/152). Two changes to the intra-body vision model: (1) the convoy beam should MOVE with a head and tail that update (not a uniformly-fading segment); (2) permanent vision as a 3-wide beam from the corp centre of operation to the market centre. Reworks the vision buffers accordingly.
items.design:
**Change 1 — moving head/tail beam.** The BL-152 buffer (per-econ-step segment flood, uniform timestamp fade) read as a chunky blob that stepped once per quarter. Replaced with a RENDER-TIME moving beam: `ui_state.convoy_beams` stores each live player intra-body convoy's tile path + progress + speed (rebuilt each frame in `update_body_vision`); the canvas interpolates a HEAD along the path by the fraction through the current econ tick (`fmod(sim_now_days,90)/90`), so it glides smoothly between quarterly steps, and trails a TAIL one econ tick's travel behind, ramping intensity 1->0 head->tail, radius-2 around each path tile. So the beam has a bright moving head and a dimming tail.

**Change 2 — permanent corp-centre->market corridors (Ben: 'from the corp centre of operation to the market centre, as a 3 wide beam').** `ui_state.permanent_vision` (non-fading) = radius-2 pockets around the player's own building tiles + 3-wide corridors (path flooded radius 1) from the corp centre of operation (lowest-id player building tile on the body, mirroring market_clearing's file-local representative_tile) to each market centre the player operates in (the catchment markets of its buildings). Always visible.

**Plumbing.** `update_body_vision` (renamed from update_convoy_vision) rebuilds both buffers per frame for the active body; moved from app::step_economy to render() (planetary branch) so the --verify capture path gets it too, and so a body switch is tracked immediately. Pathfinder is route-cache-backed (steady-state = lookups). Derived VIEW state only — no serialisation, no world/* feedback; determinism preserved.

**Render.** Fog vision = 1 in permanent_vision, else the moving beam's intensity; wash = 0.5*(1 - vision). Verified: full build clean; wide + default captures show permanent pockets/corridors lit and the globe fogged (the moving beam's motion only manifests with a live inter-market intra-body convoy, not the same-market verify seed). **Authority:** docs/ui/DISCOVERY.md.

items.title: Laws & policy surface — design + data-model stub (v0.1.2 expanded-prototype groundwork)
items.summary: Roadmap v0.1.2 expanded-prototype groundwork (Ben, 2026-07-09 refocus). First pass at the law / policy surface: what a law IS as a data object and how it gates or modifies economic (and later political) behaviour. Design-forward + data-model stub only — no committed mechanics — so the v0.2.0 nation actor and the v0.3.0 political layer land on prepared ground. Design-owed: the law-object schema, the prototype lever set, and the enforcement seam are all open.
items.design:
**Theme (roadmap v0.1.2).** Define the **law / policy** surface as a first-class data object: a law is a named, serialisable record that gates or modifies behaviour (initially economic — tax, tariff, subsidy, extraction cap — later political). This item settles the *shape*, not the mechanics.

**Scope.** Design + a data-model stub only. Enumerate the law-object schema (id, subject, condition, effect), sketch a small prototype lever set, and name the enforcement seam in the economy step where a law would read. No UI, no active law effects committed — the point is to position the model.

**Open questions.** Law-object schema; which levers are prototype-worthy vs deferred; where enforcement hooks into `economy_system` without breaking determinism; how laws relate to the future filter system (BL-087) and the nation actor (BL-094) that will own them.

**Standing-rule note.** Policy proper is post-prototype scope (TECH_FOUNDATIONS); this is the design + stub that precedes it, not the system. **Authority:** docs/SYSTEMS.md once landed.

### Shared condition-set + tangible law list (2026-07-11, mobile session, Ben)

**Object shape.** A law = **`condition_set`** (the shared predicate — see BL-156 for the full triple; here it is the enactment / applicability gate) **+ a polymorphic `effect`**. The condition side is settled by BL-156; the design genuinely new to Laws is the **effect taxonomy** and the **enforcement seam**. Both fall out of a concrete law list rather than being invented abstractly.

**Ten tangible laws (price clamps 5–6 vetoed 2026-07-11, Ben).** Grouped by effect family — the list *is* the effect taxonomy, derived from instances:

*(a) Margin modifiers — scale a flow's price/cost*
1. **Extraction tax** — per-unit levy on raw extraction output. Effect: −margin on extraction.
2. **Production subsidy** — per-unit credit on a target resource's processing. Effect: +margin / −effective input cost.
3. **Import tariff** — duty on goods arriving by convoy from off-body. Effect: +cost on inter-body imports.
4. **Export duty** — levy on goods shipped off-body. Effect: +cost on exports (retains supply locally).

*(b) Quantity clamps — bound a flow or stock*
5. **Extraction cap** — ceiling on extraction rate from a body / deposit (conservation). Effect: clamp yield.
6. **Strategic reserve mandate** — withhold N units of a resource from market before sale/export. Effect: reserve floor on stockpile.

*(c) Cost adders — per-building / per-tick overhead*
7. **Emissions levy** — cost scaling with industry density on a body (ties to the habitability feedback). Effect: +upkeep on polluting buildings.
8. **Labour-contract floor** — minimum workforce cost (minimum wage). Effect: +per-building labour cost.

*(d) Gates — binary allow/deny*
9. **Trade embargo** — ban trade of a resource, or with a named body / nation. Effect: block convoy routes for that good.
10. **Zoning restriction** — cap a building type's count per body, or ban it on a terrain class. Effect: placement-validation gate.

> Price clamps (ceiling / floor) were proposed as family (b) and **cut 2026-07-11** — the effect taxonomy now spans four families, not five. A resolved-price clamp would also be the one effect that fights the supply/demand price resolution directly rather than shifting a flow's cost; the veto keeps every law a *modifier over* the market, never an *override of* it.

Most laws are unconditional once enacted (empty `condition_set` = always-on); the interesting ones gate on world state — a **wartime tax** `(era == war)`, an **emissions levy** that only bites past an industry-density threshold `(structure-density ≥ N)`, a **reserve mandate** triggered by a market-scarcity signal `(market ≤ X)`.

**Determinism seam (the load-bearing call).** Laws are the *first* condition-set consumer a live tick reads (techs are read-only, post-prototype — BL-087 res. 6). Rules: evaluate all active laws' condition-sets at **one fixed point** in `run_economy_step`, producing a resolved modifier set *before* the step consumes it; laws touching one quantity combine **order-independently** (additive rates / defined precedence, never iteration order); `market` / `surplus` subjects read the **previous** tick's resolved values, not mid-tick mutating ones.

**Politics ≈ laws — the v0.1.2 ↔ v0.1.5 boundary (raised 2026-07-10, Ben).** A nation's political character (BL-054, `NATION_GENERATION.md`) can be expressed as a **named preset — a bundle of default law-values** — rather than a separate mechanic: a protectionist nation ships high tariffs + export duties; a statist one, price ceilings + a reserve mandate; a laissez-faire one, near-zero extraction tax + no emissions levy. This dissolves most of the BL-155 ↔ BL-158 overlap. The clean line:

- **Laws (v0.1.2)** own the **mechanism** — the modifier objects and their enforcement seam.
- **Politics (v0.1.5, BL-158)** owns two things: **(a)** named **law-bundle presets** that express character — a Laws *consumer*, not a new object; and **(b)** the inter-nation **relationship / sentiment** axis, which is genuinely *not* a law (a diplomacy state).

So the *economic-behaviour* half of a political profile is laws; only the *relationship* half is new in v0.1.5. BL-158 inherits this framing (its own field to be updated when that minor is reached — authority time-slice).

**Player levers surfaced in the Budget ledger (BL-171, 2026-07-11).** The Budget-ledger redesign ([[BL-171]]) added **Tax** and **Wages** tier selectors to the player Budget view as *stubbed* controls — drawn and selectable, no economic effect — pending this item's mechanics. Confirmed intent (Ben): **Tax** = a **player-set policy lever** (the player picks a tax tier as a deliberate trade-off); **Wages** = a **cost↔workforce trade-off** (a higher wage tier raises the wage cost but improves the workforce — availability / output / retention — moving wages from today's fixed `base_wage` constant to a player lever). These are the first two concrete laws/policies this surface must model; wire them into the ledger controls (ui_state.budget_tax_tier / budget_wage_tier, UI-only today) when this lands.

items.title: Tech system — early design toward the quest/gate model (v0.1.3 expanded-prototype groundwork)
items.summary: Roadmap v0.1.3 expanded-prototype groundwork (Ben, 2026-07-09 refocus). Early design toward the tech / quest system — the condition-set gate model (gate = quest = tech, one object) that BL-087 reframed and that the v0.3.0 filter system will formalise. Design only at this stage: settle the tech-object and gate-condition shape so later work has a spine. Precursor to BL-087 (filter system, v0.3.0).
items.design:
**Theme (roadmap v0.1.3).** The early-design pass for the **tech system**, feeding the unified gate model BL-087 settled: a **gate = quest = tech** is one condition-set object, so a tech can gate on economic OR world state. This item does the groundwork design; BL-087 formalises it as the filter system in v0.3.0.

**Scope.** Design only — no implementation. Settle the tech / gate-condition object shape, the capstone-vs-ordinary distinction, and how a tech unlock threads into content availability (buildings, recipes, quest trees). Position it so v0.3.0's Era→Filter rename inherits a coherent model.

**Open questions.** Tech-object schema and its overlap with the law object (BL-155); which conditions are expressible in the prototype; how quest trees hang off capstones; the boundary between this precursor and BL-087's full design.

**Relates:** BL-087 (filter system, v0.3.0 — this is its early-design precursor), BL-155 (shared condition-set shape). **Authority:** docs/SYSTEMS.md once landed.

### Shared condition-set — the tech/law predicate unified (2026-07-11, mobile session, Ben)

The 2026-07-08 tech mock (`world/tech_tree.{hpp,cpp}`) stores `condition` as a **single label** (`research | structure | stockpile | market | surplus | era`) — descriptive, not evaluable. BL-155 (Laws) forces the promotion: a law is read every tick and must resolve true/false, so the label must become a **structured predicate**. Settled shape, shared by tech / quest / law / (v0.3.0) filter:

- **`condition_set` = a flat AND-list of atomic conditions** — no nested OR-mesh (mirrors BL-087 resolution 1: binary tree, no re-converging mesh). Keeps evaluation order deterministic and the predicate legible.
- **atomic condition = `(subject, comparator, threshold, sustained_ticks)`**:
  - `subject` — the 2026-07-08 vocabulary reused verbatim: `research` (tech id complete) · `structure` (building exists / count) · `stockpile` (resource ≥ N) · `market` (price / volume signal) · `surplus` (sustained net-positive flow) · `era` (world clock ≥ Era N) · `line-depth` (standing-line tier ≥ N).
  - `comparator` — `≥ / ≤ / == / exists`.
  - `threshold` — number, resource id, tech id, or era ordinal.
  - `sustained_ticks` — default 0 (instantaneous); >0 = must hold N ticks. The Propellant Loop capstone's "sustained surplus" is `(surplus, ≥, X, N)`.

The `condition` **label** already on `tech_node` becomes the `subject` axis of this triple — the vocabulary was the hard part and it is done; this only makes it evaluable. **Effect stays polymorphic** (see BL-155): tech → discrete unlock, quest → opens next tree, law → continuous modifier, filter → availability window. One condition type, many effect types. Direct precursor to BL-087's filter system, which inherits this predicate wholesale.

items.title: Automatic exchange policy — per-resource auto-buy/sell bands (blacklist-default) + relocate sell orders to the market surface
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-09 (Ben, market-exchanges design session; all forks settled by Q&A). The player governor over the already-automatic order book: standing per-(corp,body,resource) inventory-band policies that shape what the auto path does with the player's own stock, blacklist-default, surfaced as a new Market Ledger 'Policy' view. Retires the construction-panel Sell Orders tab into it (BL-143 companion). Axis A of automatic exchanges; Axis B (counterparty) is fast-follow BL-161. v0.2, after the prototype cut.
items.design:
**Settled 2026-07-09 (Ben, market-exchanges design session; five forks resolved via Q&A).** The order book already auto-derives BOTH sides each tick (clear_markets: pool surplus above production auto-sells; processor input shortfalls auto-buy). This item adds the PLAYER GOVERNOR on top — standing policies that bound what the automatic path may do with the player's own stock — and retires the manual sell-order tab into it.

**Axis A — per (player-corp, body, resource) inventory-band policy (the FULL band, Ben's call):** `sell_enabled` + `reserve` (hold >= this; auto-sell only the surplus above reserve + next-run production need) + `floor_price`; `buy_enabled` + `target` (auto-buy UP TO this stock level — speculative stockpiling for a construction draw / a planned convoy, MAY exceed production need) + `ceiling_price`. Between reserve and target: hold. Today's manual sell order is the degenerate one-tick case (enabled, reserve 0, floor).

**Default polarity — BLACKLIST-DEFAULT (Ben's call).** Unconfigured resources auto-trade exactly as today; every player action is subtractive/bounding (blacklist = sell_enabled false -> hold; band = set reserve/target/limits). No dead market on ship day — the current substrate IS the default.

**Mechanism.** A new `derive_exchange_orders(w, policies)` runs each econ tick BEFORE clear_markets, reading policy + current pool + production need and emitting the `player_orders`/`player_buy_orders` overlay that clear_markets ALREADY accepts — no order-book core change. Fully deterministic (world/* standing rule).

**Hard constraint — local-body only, never auto-launches.** SUPPLY.md: space launches are ALWAYS player-directed. Auto-buy-to-target may be satisfied only from the SAME body's market; a policy can never trigger an inter-body convoy. Cross-body acquisition stays a manual convoy decision. (Same-body terrestrial auto-dispatch already exists in the substrate, so this is consistent, not new.)

**Serialisation seam.** Policies are player-authored world state -> a new serialised policy table (flat binary, no SQLite). This makes the item Full-mode, determinism- + save-format-touching; needs a verifier-headless check on derive_exchange_orders and a save round-trip.

**Surface — new Market Ledger 'Policy' view (Ben's call)** beside Prices/Markets/Trends: one inline-editable row per resource (Resource | Sell | Reserve | Floor | Buy | Target | Ceiling) for the selected body's player pool. This is BL-143's 'relocate sell orders to the market surface' home, so REMOVING the construction panel's Sell Orders tab (draw_sell_orders_section) is a REQUIRED companion here — couples to BL-143 (which independently wants that tab gone).

**Scope / sequence.** v0.2 — Ben pushed the whole automatic-exchange feature PAST the prototype cut; v0.1.0 stays audit-only and playtest ships on the current auto-derived substrate without the policy layer. Axis B (counterparty allow/deny — the embargo/Trade->Conflict lever) is the cross-linked fast-follow BL-161.

**Authority** -> docs/SYSTEMS.md § Trade (mechanic) + docs/ui/ledgers/market.md (surface) on landing.

**AI-primitive confirmation (2026-07-26, AI design session).** The inventory-band policy table is also the AI's trade surface: AI corps author the same per-(corp, body, resource) policies via the corp_command seam (AI_OPPONENT.md §5-6) - there is no AI-only trade path. derive_exchange_orders must therefore read policies for ALL corps, not just the player (same mechanism, same determinism; the player UI is just one author of many).

items.title: Counterparty allow/deny — embargo & exclusive-trade lever (automatic exchanges, Axis B)
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-09 (Ben, market-exchanges design session). Axis B of automatic exchanges — the counterparty control, and the half that turns Trade into a Conflict lever. Per-(player-corp) allow/deny list of rival corps, applied as a match filter; deny-list = embargo, allow-list = exclusive trade. fast-follow to BL-160; realises the counterparty-preference open Brief in SYSTEMS.md § Trade. v0.2.
items.design:
**Settled 2026-07-09 (Ben, market-exchanges design session).** Axis B of automatic exchanges — the counterparty control, and the half that makes Trade a Conflict lever. Fast-follow to BL-160 (Axis A resource bands); realises the 'counterparty preference' open Brief in SYSTEMS.md § Trade.

**Model.** A per (player-corp) allow/deny list of rival corps, applied as a filter inside clear_markets' matching loop (skip disallowed (buyer, seller) pairs). Two modes: DENY-LIST (the common case — refuse to match a named rival: an embargo) and ALLOW-LIST (the extreme — trade ONLY with named corps: an exclusive supply relationship). Complements the existing soft `preferred_seller` +10% tie-hint with a HARD include/exclude.

**Surface.** The action lives on the RIVAL's Selection panel ('Embargo / Trade-only') — where the player is already looking at that competitor (BL-093 made Selection action-first). The BL-160 Policy view reflects the resulting state.

**Serialisation.** The counterparty list is player-authored world state -> serialised alongside the BL-160 policy table (flat binary).

**Scope / sequence.** v0.2, after BL-160 — requires its derive/overlay plumbing.

**Authority** -> docs/SYSTEMS.md § Trade on landing.

**AI-primitive confirmation (2026-07-26, AI design session).** The allow/deny list is per-corp, not player-only: AI corps embargo via the same corp_command verb (AI_OPPONENT.md §5), making embargoes a symmetric Trade->Conflict lever. An AI-initiated embargo should surface in the BL-205 chat log (public channel) - diplomacy as legible messaging, not hidden state.

items.title: Tile-specific construction panel — mirrors the tile Selection element but charts expected profit, and actually builds
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-10 (Ben, during the BL-123 tile-Selection redesign). The tile Selection element's 'Construct Buildings' button currently routes to the existing Construction panel, which does NOT let you construct on the selected tile — a dead-end. Ben wants a dedicated tile-construction panel, laid out like the new tile Selection element (BL-123) but with a chart of each candidate building's EXPECTED PROFIT in place of the deposit bars, and which actually performs the build on that tile. This is where the BL-071 placement-suitability affordances (Thrives/Valid/Invalid) belong now that they've left the Selection panel. Design-owed on Ben's mockup for the panel's proportions.
items.design:
**Filed 2026-07-10 (Ben, during the BL-123 tile-Selection redesign). Design-owed on Ben's mockup.**

### Problem
The redesigned tile Selection element (BL-123) leads its 2x2 button grid with **Construct Buildings**, which today stubs onto `ui.show_construction_panel` — the existing Construction panel. Ben's finding: that panel *does not actually allow construction on the selected tile* — the entry point routes back to a surface that can't build. The construction front door is broken.

### Wanted
A **tile-specific construction panel** that:
- Is laid out **like the tile Selection element** (BL-123 vertical stack), so the two read as a family.
- **Replaces the deposit bars with an expected-profit chart** — one bar per placeable building type (or per candidate recipe), showing the estimated net/tick that building would earn on THIS tile (reuse `estimate_building_profit` / `building_profit.hpp`, the seam the building Selection facts already use).
- **Actually performs the build** — choosing an affordable type enqueues the construction request (the `construct_building` path), which the current panel fails to do from the tile entry.
- **Carries the BL-071 placement affordances** (Thrives / Valid / Invalid, reason-coded) — their home now that they no longer render on the Selection panel (see SELECTION.md § The tile element's layout).

### Relationships
Follows **BL-123** (the tile Selection layout it mirrors and is reached from). Consumes **BL-044** (full construction cost: budget + materials), **BL-071** (placement_rules affordance seam), **BL-074** (`estimate_building_profit`). Supersedes the Construct Buildings stub wired in BL-123.

### Method
Ben supplies a mockup for the panel's proportions (per the visual-design-with-Ben convention); coding follows. Likely a new surface in `construction_panel.cpp` (or a sibling) opened by the tile panel's Construct Buildings button in place of the current `show_construction_panel` stub. Authority `docs/ui/SELECTION.md` (+ MENU.md for the construction surface) on landing.

items.title: On-canvas legends need smooth scrolling for overflowing entry lists
items.completion_note: Landed 2026-07-10 (also resolves [[BL-163]], folded per Ben). Added a shared draw_scroll_list_key helper in body_surface_canvas.cpp: a dark panel with a fixed header (+ optional good-selector combo for the Market lens) over a bounded, wheel/drag-scrolling borderless ImGui child hosting the rows (the draw_lens_resource_combo pattern). Box height is capped to the canvas vertical span [grid_top+8, canvas_bottom-8] passed from the caller and clamped in-bounds, so a long list scrolls instead of overrunning. Goldens for the changed lenses (country_lens, market_lens, and reach/supply where the key renders) need re-blessing on Linux CI — the change is intentional. Authority propagated to LENSES.md.
items.summary: Filed 2026-07-10 (Ben ideas thread). Legends in general (the on-canvas lens legends in body_surface_canvas.cpp) should scroll smoothly when their entry list exceeds the available height, rather than overflowing or being clipped. Generalises the fix in [[BL-163]] from the Resource lens to all lens legends.
items.design: **Give the on-canvas lens legends a scrollable body.** Where a legend's entry list can exceed the reserved height (Country with many nations, Market with many markets, Resource with deposit bands), host the entry rows in a bounded, smoothly-scrolling ImGui child (window flags for a clean scrollbar; the existing scrollable BeginCombo at body_surface_canvas.cpp:137 is precedent for hosting scroll chrome inside a legend). Keep the legend header/title fixed and scroll only the rows. Smooth (pixel/wheel) scroll, not paged. Shared helper across the per-lens legend builders so the behaviour is uniform.
