Fairness clauses inherited from persona-runtime.md: blackboard-only reads, fixed compute budget, seeded determinism, exploitability. FIRST SLICE: pack loader + the mountain bench (sun-tzu/amaterasu/krishna) + Counsel channel feed. Requirement (headless, tools/verify/persona_counsel_harness.cpp): two corps, same seed, an alignment dilemma (the strong-vs-weak precedent, Pantheon session 2026-07-26); assert (1) byte-identical opinion logs across two runs, (2) blackboard-only reads (no world pointer in the Lua env), (3) at least one inter-bench disagreement resolved by an explicit verdict record.

items.title: World history log — an append-only narrative substrate replacing the per-eval blackboard snapshot (enables a past-history game mode)
items.summary: Ben's pivot (2026-07-28), reacting to BL-206's snapshot-style blackboard export: re-deriving a fresh state summary from the world every time someone reads it is 'unnecessary and boring overhead.' Proposal: make the append-only EVENT LOG the source of truth from world generation onward, not a per-eval snapshot query. Concretely, the bones already exist and are scattered: corp_ai's decision ring (corp_decision_ring) is already an event log of AI commands; trade_routes (last_tick, convoy_count) is already history, not state; agency_event is already a live narrated feed; and PLANETOLOGY.md's per-body dated biography (S0-S9, already implemented under BL-167 - abiogenesis at S5 Spark, the oxygenation bottlenecks at S6 Breath, land colonisation at S7 Green) is already exactly 'how chemical life started and what evolution bottlenecks led to humans forming,' produced once at generation and never revisited. This item unifies those into one growing, replayable log spanning generation through simulation, with the corp_ai blackboard snapshot and the BL-206 JSONL export becoming a DERIVED VIEW over the log rather than an authored artifact. The payoff Ben named: a game can start reading the log from tick 0 instead of 'now,' which is most of what a 'play through the past' mode needs, close to free once the log is the substrate.
items.design: NOT YET DESIGNED IN DETAIL - captured per Rule 0a (save now, detail later). Ben's explicit sequencing (2026-07-28): the abiogenesis/evolution-bottleneck history (BL-167/PLANETOLOGY.md S5-S8) must be solid BEFORE building the storytelling/log architecture on top of it - confirm/extend that chain first; do not treat it as a placeholder to fill in later. Open questions for the real design pass: (1) do persona/blackboard consumers keep querying a derived snapshot (recommended - cheapest, and the snapshot becomes disposable rather than authored), or move to reasoning over deltas since last read (more powerful, more stateful, larger rewrite of scripts/personas/*.lua's extract() contract); (2) what the log's storage shape is (per-body vs per-corp vs a single interleaved world log; append-only in memory only, or serialised - no serialiser exists in the repo today per PLANETOLOGY.md's own note); (3) how PLANETOLOGY.md's per-body dated lines (currently inline on body_component, 'no serialiser exists... constraint later') become the log's genesis chapter rather than a one-shot report string; (4) how a 'past' game mode actually plays - passive readback vs a played-through interstitial campaign; (5) reconciling with GENERATION_LEDGER.md's already-designed per-tile derivation breadcrumb, which is the same instinct (explain what happened and why) scoped to tuning rather than narrative. Read AI_OPPONENT.md S6 (state export), GENERATION_LEDGER.md, and PLANETOLOGY.md S Presentation before designing.

items.title: Molecular event trace for abiogenesis — full chemical-synthesis-to-DNA log per body, persisted binary, hex-inspectable, chemical-name display
items.summary: DESIGNED 2026-07-28. Promotes the chemistry currently sitting in COMMENTS at planetology.cpp S5/S6 into a generated, branching, inspectable molecular event trace. S5 Spark today is one boolean emitting one history line; this decomposes it into seven independently-failing gates (Feedstock / Reductant / Phosphorylation / Concentration / Replicator / Compartment / Code) running chemical-synthesis -> RNA -> DNA, and puts a cofactor fork in front of S6's existing flux-balance test. The highest-value piece: the PHOTOSYSTEM FORK (anoxygenic photoferrotrophy vs oxygenic Z-scheme, gated on manganese for the Mn4CaO5 complex) converts PLANETOLOGY.md's own named 'Known weaknesses' uncertainty — whether banded iron gates on life or on oxygen — from a constant into a generated branch. Several gates reach BACK into S0-S4 rolls (S1's late veneer now feeds S5a's impact-reducing atmosphere and S5c's schreibersite phosphorus), which is what makes generation read as one causal system rather than ten independent dice. Adds 3 archetypes (Silent Eden, RNA Lock, Ferrotroph World). Storage is 8-byte fixed-width flat-binary events referencing compiled-in species/reaction tables — ids never strings, so hex is purely a dev display encoding and canonical chemical names resolve through the same table any player surface uses (~500 bytes/body). Q&A 2026-07-28 settled: generative full 7-gate chain (not explanatory-only), new archetypes, drill-down behind the untouched eight-line biography, and design-now/build-after-BL-208.
items.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-28 (Ben, Q&A). Four calls settled: (a) GENERATIVE, FULL 7-GATE CHAIN - every sub-gate can fail independently and change the endowment, not merely narrate an existing verdict; (b) NEW ARCHETYPES added rather than folding new outcomes into the existing 13; (c) surfaced as a DRILL-DOWN behind the eight-line biography, which stays exactly as-is (PLANETOLOGY.md's eight-line cap is load-bearing - the brevity of a failed world IS its characterisation); (d) DESIGN NOW, BUILD AFTER BL-208, so the trace is authored as entries in the append-only world log rather than a parallel per-body structure.

## The problem being solved

S5 Spark is currently ONE BOOLEAN at planetology.cpp:780 - `cycling_venue && geology >= low && time_budget && rng < abiogenesis_ease` - emitting one history line. All the real chemistry (serpentinisation H2, the 0.1 M HCN threshold, Fe(Ni)S walls matching ferredoxin) lives in COMMENTS, not in data. This item promotes that chemistry into a generated, branching, inspectable trace.

## S5 decomposed into seven gates

Each reads inputs already computed by earlier stages, tests one threshold, and has a distinct failure state. Several reach BACK into S0-S4 rolls, which is the point: it makes generation read as one causal system rather than ten independent dice.

| Gate | Question | Key chemistry | Reads from | Fails into |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S5a Feedstock | Anything to build with? | HCN -> purines (adenine is literally (HCN)5); HCHO -> sugars via formose. Yield collapses orders of magnitude in an oxidised CO2/N2 atmosphere vs a reduced one. Modern resolution: IMPACT-GENERATED TRANSIENT REDUCING ATMOSPHERES - a large iron-rich impactor reduces H2O to H2 for ~10^5-10^6 yr (Zahnle, Genda). | S2 atmosphere class; **S1 late-veneer roll**; UV flux | sterile - no organic feedstock, ever |
| S5b Reductant | Free energy of the right shape? | Serpentinisation: olivine + H2O -> serpentine + magnetite + H2, exothermic. Lost City runs 45-90 C, pH 9-11, up to 200 mM H2. Alkaline effluent into a CO2-acidified ocean = a 3-4 pH-unit gradient of the same polarity every living cell uses, across Fe(Ni)S walls. | S3 geology; S4 liquid water; ultramafic crust from S1 | prebiotic - feedstock present, nothing to cycle it |
| S5c Phosphorylation | Could it make a nucleotide? | The genuinely hard one. Seawater P ~1 uM, locked in apatite. Two routes: SCHREIBERSITE (Fe3P from iron meteorites) corroding to reactive phosphite; or CARBONATE-RICH ALKALINE LAKES where Ca drops out as carbonate, freeing P to concentrate ~10^5-10^6x (Toner & Catling). | **S1 metallic impactors** (schreibersite); **S4 subaerial relief + evaporation** (lakes) | NEW: monomers, no nucleotides - sugars and bases exist, nothing links them |
| S5d Concentration | Dense enough to polymerise? | HCN oligomerises above ~0.1 M, competes with hydrolysis at 0.01-0.1 M, loses below. Hadean ocean HCN was orders of magnitude under. 'The ocean was a soup' is chemically false. Venues: wet-dry cycling in subaerial pools (dehydration drives condensation - polymerisation in bulk water is uphill), or hydrothermal pore thermophoresis (~5000x, Braun & Mast), which works WITHOUT land. | S4 water_fraction, relief; S3 geology | prebiotic - today's outcome, now with a named cause |
| S5e Replicator | Did a polymer copy itself AND survive? | THE NEW PHYSICS: an RNA temperature ceiling. The phosphodiester backbone hydrolyses, and the rate climbs steeply with temperature - order-of-magnitude, hours at ~100 C against years near 0 C; cytosine deamination is worse. This sets up a DIRECT ANTAGONISM WITH S5b: vents give the reductant and the gradient, and vents are hot. Lost City at 45-90 C is survivable; a black smoker at 350 C is not. | S4 surface_temp_k; vent temp from S3 theta; S5d venue | NEW: polymers, no replicator - 'chemistry got further here than anywhere else, and stopped' |
| S5f Compartment | Did it become an individual? | Fatty-acid vesicles self-assemble above a critical concentration; without one, a useful ribozyme's benefit diffuses to its competitors and there is no Darwinian individuality. Known unresolved tension: fatty-acid membranes are destabilised by divalent cations, and RNA catalysis REQUIRES Mg2+. Chelators (citrate) are the proposed workaround. | ocean divalent-cation load, from S4 weathering + S1 crust | NEW: replicators, no cells |
| S5g Code | Did it lift the genome ceiling? | RNA -> coded protein (the ribosome is itself a ribozyme) -> DNA via ribonucleotide reductase. The real constraint is EIGEN'S ERROR THRESHOLD: without proofreading, max genome length ~ 1/(per-base mutation rate), capping an RNA-only replicator near a few thousand bases. DNA plus a proofreading polymerase lifts that by orders of magnitude. | S5e fidelity; time budget; cofactors | NEW: RNA LOCK - real, metabolising, evolving life, permanently simple |

**S5f is the weakest of the seven on the 'name the decision' test** - its failure state is exotic and its downstream endowment is identical to S5e's. It is included because Ben chose the full chain, but it is explicitly THE FIRST CANDIDATE TO CUT if tuning shows it never fires distinctly from S5e.

## S6 - the photosystem fork (the highest-value piece)

This converts a named uncertainty in PLANETOLOGY.md's own 'Known weaknesses' into a GENERATED BRANCH instead of a constant. The doc says the BIF oxidant is 'genuinely unresolved between cyanobacterial O2, anoxygenic photoferrotrophy (which needs no free oxygen at all) and abiotic UV photo-oxidation, AND IT DECIDES WHETHER BIF GATES ON LIFE OR ON OXYGEN' - which is what the whole iron/coal antagonism hangs on.

- **S6a Anoxygenic photosynthesis (photoferrotrophy).** One photosystem, Fe(II) as electron donor, no O2 produced. Cheap - fires on nearly any microbial world with dissolved iron. **Precipitates banded iron with NO free oxygen at all.**
- **S6b Oxygenic photosynthesis.** Splitting water needs +1.23 V, more than any single photosystem delivers - which is why it needs TWO chained in series (the Z-scheme), and why it evolved exactly once in 4 Gyr on Earth. Its cofactor is the Mn4CaO5 oxygen-evolving complex, so it GATES ON MANGANESE. Requires the genome headroom from S5g (two photosystems + dozens of genes is not reachable under an RNA-world error threshold).
- **S6c Nitrogen fixation.** N2's 941 kJ/mol triple bond yields only to nitrogenase, whose cofactor is Mo - soluble in oxic water, NOT in anoxic sulfidic water. Low Mo -> weak fixation -> capped productivity -> capped burial -> capped oxygen; and since S8 already states soil requires biological nitrogen fixation, **Mo gates arable_share through pure chemistry.**

The existing GOE / Boring Billion / NOE flux-balance structure runs UNDERNEATH this, unchanged. The cofactor gates sit in front of it.

**Mo and P stay INTERNAL SCALARS, never resources** - this deliberately does not touch PLANETOLOGY.md open call 3 (resource-list expansion), which would shift resource_count and every std::array width in the model.

## New archetypes (13 -> 16)

| Archetype | Died at | Has | Lacks |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Silent Eden** | S5c or S5e, on an otherwise perfect world | oceans, continents, mild climate, pristine ore unweathered by life, clay, sand | ALL fossil carbon, all biology, and - via S8's nitrogen-fixation requirement - **soil: land you cannot farm despite perfect climate** |
| **RNA Lock** | S5g | a real microbial biosphere, marine organics, some BIF | any complexity, any oxygen, any path forward |
| **Ferrotroph World** | S6b (cofactor/genome), with S6a fired | colossal UNBOUNDED banded iron - the window never closes | oxygen, permanently and structurally |

**Silent Eden is the most valuable of the three.** Today a perfect wet world that never sparked resolves to relict_wet, which is WRONG - relict_wet is Mars, a world that lost its air. A living-capable world that stayed silent is a different thing entirely and the current model cannot name it.

**Honest risk on Ferrotroph World:** it may be indistinguishable from Mat World to a player. Both read iron-rich and anoxic. The real difference is causal - Mat World failed on FLUX BALANCE (the reductant flux won, and falling theta could in principle have fixed it), Ferrotroph failed on BIOCHEMISTRY (it never built the water-splitting complex; there is no path). Differentiate them mechanically by giving Ferrotroph a strictly higher, never-closing iron window, plus its own blurb. If tuning cannot separate them, fold Ferrotroph into Mat World rather than shipping two names for one feeling.

## Data model

The compression insight is NOT hex - it is that an event stores IDs and the stoichiometry lives in a static compiled-in table. Hex text is ~2x the size of binary and buys nothing as storage; it is purely a DISPLAY encoding for the dev inspector.

```
struct molecular_event   // 8 bytes, flat binary, fixed width
{
    uint16_t epoch_myr;  // Myr before present / 10 - covers 655 Gyr
    uint8_t  process_id; // index into reaction_table
    uint8_t  outcome;    // fired / marginal / failed / bypassed
    uint16_t yield_q;    // fixed-point, 1/1000
    uint8_t  venue_id;   // vent / pool / pore / lake / subsurface
    uint8_t  flags;
};
```

Two tables in `src/world/chemistry_tables.{hpp,cpp}`, compiled in and NEVER serialised:
- `species_table[]` - id, formula ('HCN'), canonical name ('hydrogen cyanide'), class (feedstock / reductant / monomer / polymer / cofactor / waste). ~35 entries.
- `reaction_table[]` - id, name ('serpentinisation'), reactant ids, product ids, one prose line, owning sub-gate. ~25 entries.

**An event never holds a string.** The hex inspector and any player-facing surface both decode through the SAME table, so names cannot drift from ids and raw bytes can never leak to display. Rendered form:

```
3F 0C 01 4E 20 02 00 00
  3.90 Gya  serpentinisation   FIRED   yield 0.31   venue: alkaline vent
            olivine + H2O -> serpentine + magnetite + H2
```

Budget: ~60 events on a living world, ~10 on a dead one -> **under 500 bytes per body**, comfortably inside the envelope PLANETOLOGY.md already reserves (~120 bytes + a <=64-byte event array).

## Determinism

- **Seven new stage tags** for the RNG sub-streams, plus 2-3 for the S6 sub-gates. Existing tags are tag_accretion 0x51A1, tag_breath 0xB6EA, tag_green 0x67EE, and an inline 0x5A4B at S5. Allocate FRESH constants; PLANETOLOGY.md warns 0x4A71012u is already folded twice in hard_coded_world.cpp.
- **Per-sub-gate hashed sub-streams are load-bearing here**, more than anywhere else in the model: they are what lets a later gate be added or retuned without silently re-rolling every earlier one.
- **The RNA hydrolysis temperature curve MUST be a lookup table**, not exp(). Arrhenius kinetics in a gate path is exactly the portability hazard PLANETOLOGY.md names - exp/log/pow are not bit-identical across compilers, libm versions or fast-math settings. Specify a 16-entry table over 0-160 C, on the precedent of the radiogenic decay already binned at 0.05 Gyr.
- **This is also why the kinetic-network depth was rejected.** Integrating real concentrations over time is nothing BUT exponentials in gate paths; it would need every rate as a lookup, arriving at this design with ~200 free parameters and four calibration bodies.

## Harness impact (tools/verify/planetology_harness.cpp)

**Blast radius is smaller than it looks: three of the four prototype bodies die at S1-S3 and never reach S5, and the fourth (Kepler) is the constrained homeworld the strict floor forces through.**

| Group | Risk |
|---|---|
| R2 four bodies land in stated archetypes | LOW - Kepler must still be Cradle; the floor enforces it |
| R3 B->C joint | unchanged |
| R4 iron/coal antagonism | **AT RISK** - the photosystem fork adds a second, independent iron pathway; re-assert both ends |
| R5 homeworld corridor 100/100 | **AT RISK** - seven new gates the homeworld must clear; acceptance rate will fall, reject-and-reroll absorbs it, but planetology_sweep MUST re-measure per-lean cost so no preference becomes a dead end |
| R7 every knob moves its outcome | new cofactor gates need their own assertions |
| **R12 NEW - the trace** | event sequence is deterministic in (seed, body); and EVERY emitted species/reaction id resolves in the table (no orphan ids). The orphan-id check is the key new invariant, since ids and names are now decoupled |

`abiogenesis_ease` should now bias the WHOLE chain rather than a single draw at S5. No new player knob is proposed - the existing eight preferences already cover the axes, and PLANETOLOGY.md's rule is that a knob must change something a player can read.

## Cut, by the diagnostic test

PLANETOLOGY.md: 'for every generated value, name the decision it changes. Anything that fails is deleted, not tuned.' Cut: **homochirality** (beautiful, names no decision); **nucleobase route** - formamide vs cyanosulfidic vs HCN (three paths, identical output; may survive as flavour naming only); **panspermia** (moves the question, changes nothing); **LUCA's gene set** (invisible downstream); **eukaryogenesis** (borderline - overlaps Boring Billion's 'oxygen present and useless'; revisit only if the Boring Billion outcome proves too rare).

## Residual calls (implementation-time, with recommendations)

1. **Manganese is not currently derived anywhere.** S6b needs it. Recommend a crustal-Mn scalar from metallicity x crustal reworking - cheap, and it reuses S0's one-nebula correlation.
2. **S5f Compartment** - cut if it never fires distinctly from S5e (see above).
3. **Ferrotroph vs Mat World separation** - fold if tuning cannot distinguish them.
4. **Authority propagation:** PLANETOLOGY.md is deliberately NOT edited by this entry. Per the standing rule, a settled design for an open item lives in the item until the work lands, then propagates into the authority doc as part of landing it.

Read PLANETOLOGY.md S5/S6/S8, 'Determinism & cost', 'Known weaknesses' and 'Presentation' in full before promoting.

items.title: Generation pivot — one continuous simulated oral history from S0 to the 1900s, with extinction-event branching and a batch-tuning sweep
items.progress_note:
FIRST SLICE LANDED 2026-07-28: Continents/Drift sibling pass (src/world/continents.{hpp,cpp}) — plate count/drift/speed derived from Planetology's mobile_lid/theta (a consequence, not a roll), Voronoi-assigned per tile, boundary dot-product classifies convergent (uplift, arc-magmatism note) vs divergent (rift, new-coastline note), history_event lines merge into the body biography tagged chain_stage::engine. Wired into generate_body_tiles via an optional continent_bias param (null preserves the pre-BL-210 surface bit-for-bit). Verified by tools/verify/continents_harness.cpp (R1-R5: determinism, plate-count bound, stagnant-lid special case, both boundary signs fire across a seed spread, every line carries a consequence) — all PASS. Regression-checked against determinism_harness, world_audit, and planetology_harness — all green (world_audit's S2 forest+wetland threshold required tuning the bias magnitude down 3x from the first pass, since the original 0.30/0.15/0.35/0.25 constants visibly disrupted Kepler's existing terrain balance — corrected to 0.10/0.05/0.12/0.08). NOT YET DONE: the checkpoint/branch mechanism (still pure per-pair classification, no lean hook-in yet), Nations/Corporations rewrite, the batch-sweep extension, and TILE_GENERATION.md/NATION_GENERATION.md/CORPORATION_GENERATION.md doc updates recording any of this as settled authority (per the standing rule, authority docs are not touched until the work lands as a whole item, not slice-by-slice).

SPLIT 2026-07-31 (Sprint 2 planning): the three remaining not-yet-settled subject-doc passes this item's own summary predicted would split off have been filed as their own design-owed items, sequenced by real dependency rather than left flat inside this umbrella: BL-217 (checkpoint/branch data model - foundational, no dependency beyond BL-167), BL-218 (Nations rewrite - requires BL-217, DEVLOG's named 'biggest remaining piece'), BL-219 (Corporations rewrite - requires BL-218, consumes its output). This item (BL-210) now tracks as the umbrella closing condition: it stays open until BL-217/218/219 are all built AND the batch-sweep extension + authority-doc propagation (TILE_GENERATION/NATION_GENERATION/CORPORATION_GENERATION) land as this item's own final closing step.
items.summary: UMBRELLA, DESIGN-OWED 2026-07-28 (Ben session). Reframes generation from four separate mechanisms (planetology chain -> mechanical 6-pass tiles -> Voronoi nations -> focus-table corporations) into ONE continuous simulated history: S1-S4 continents become an actual plate-drift/collision/rift simulation (subsuming BL-051's parked speculative tectonics half) instead of noise/heightmap; the existing S5-S8 biosphere chain (BL-167, extended by BL-209's 7-gate S5/S6) stays the proven template; and a NEW settlement -> industrialisation -> 1900s stage replaces NATION_GENERATION's Voronoi BFS and CORPORATION_GENERATION's authored focus tables with simulated nation/corporate emergence. Extinction-class events (mass extinctions already narrated today, plus new 'historical extinction' analogues - collapses, wars) become BRANCH CHECKPOINTS: the existing world_preferences lean mechanism (BL-167 Round A/B/C) extends to bias which branch fires at each checkpoint, replacing pure reject-and-reroll with reject-reroll-or-branch. The multi-world batch tool (today's planetology_sweep.cpp, sampling seeds) becomes a BRANCH-COMBINATION sweep: it explores lean x checkpoint-branch space, not just seeds, to find which combinations reliably produce good (viable, varied, interesting) worlds - this is the mechanism for tuning target parameters that the user asked for, and it directly answers PLANETOLOGY.md's own named gap ('the pass hands nothing to nation or corporation generation... the largest missing connection'). Deepest-rung choice confirmed 3x by Ben over the narrate-on-top / mechanical-stays / offline-tool-only alternatives (see ben-picks-the-deeper-option memory). This is an UMBRELLA item: each subject doc (TILE_GENERATION continents, NATION_GENERATION/CORPORATION_GENERATION settlement-to-1900s, the checkpoint/branch mechanism itself) needs its own design pass and will likely split into per-doc sub-items once each is settled, same pattern BL-167 followed before it implemented.
items.design:
ARCHITECTURE PROPOSED 2026-07-28, NOT YET SETTLED PER SUBJECT DOC. This entry records the cross-doc shape agreed in session; each subject doc still needs its own design conversation before promotion (see summary).

## Why now

GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's ordering today is four independent mechanisms glued together: planetology (BL-167) runs a real S0-S9 causal chain per body and stops at 'now'; TILE_GENERATION's six-pass pipeline reads planetology's output but is otherwise noise/heightmap/cluster-based, not itself historical; NATION_GENERATION places territory by Voronoi BFS over the tile map, deriving resource profile by summing deposits; CORPORATION_GENERATION places lean specialist holdings by an authored focus table. PLANETOLOGY.md's own 'Known weaknesses' section already names the seam: 'the pass hands nothing to nation or corporation generation... arable share, river connectivity, fossil geography and ore provinces are exactly what should seed Voronoi nation placement and corporate industrial focus... this is the largest missing connection and it is not a small follow-on.' This item is that follow-on, taken to its full depth rather than a patch.

## The new pipeline shape

One continuous simulated history with checkpoints, replacing the current planetology -> tiles -> nations -> corporations handoff:

```
S0 System (unchanged, one campaign-wide roll)
S1-S4 Continents  <- NEW: actual plate drift / collision / rift simulation.
  Terrain is an OUTPUT of this simulated history, not a noise/heightmap pass reading
  static solar parameters. Subsumes BL-051's parked 'speculative orbital-derivation +
  tectonic landforms' half (that item's buildable cosmetic half - band smoothing,
  coastline refinement - is untouched and stays a separate, already-promote-ready sibling pass).
  checkpoint: water-gate / ice-age branch (S4's existing Oven/Snowball/Relict failures,
  reframed as branch points a lean can bias rather than pure reject-reroll)
S5-S8 Biosphere (existing BL-167 chain, extended by BL-209's 7-gate S5/S6 - REUSED AS THE
  PROVEN TEMPLATE, not rewritten)
  checkpoint: mass-extinction branch (already narrated in the eight-line biography today,
  e.g. '252 Mya extinction, recovery took ten million years' - promoted from flavour text
  to an actual branch point)
Settlement -> Industrialisation -> 1900s  <- NEW: replaces NATION_GENERATION's Voronoi BFS
  and CORPORATION_GENERATION's focus tables. Nation territory, political character, and
  corporate industrial focus become OUTPUTS of a simulated settlement/conflict/
  industrialisation history, seeded by the continent and biosphere history above (arable
  share, river connectivity, ore provinces, fossil geography) rather than summed post-hoc
  from tile deposits.
  checkpoint: 'historical extinction' branch (collapse, war, revolution - the historical-
  scale analogue of a mass extinction; also where the post-WW2 industrial grounding open
  item in GENERATION_STRATEGY.md finally gets a mechanism rather than staying an unsettled
  research note)
```

## The checkpoint/branch/lean mechanism

Extends BL-167's already-shipped preferences design (eight axes, each a lean of any/low/mid/high, resolved from the seed via reject-and-reroll, never directly editable - 'if you have preferences you can find them, but really you don't get full customization') rather than inventing a new UI concept. Today a lean narrows a sampling range within ONE round; this generalises it so a lean can also bias WHICH branch fires at a checkpoint (e.g. a 'turbulent' historical lean makes a war-branch more likely at a settlement checkpoint, without ever letting the player type a probability). The existing reject-and-reroll discipline is preserved exactly - a branch is proposed, evaluated against viability floors (the homeworld-viability pattern from BL-167), and rerolled if it fails, never clamped.

## The batch-tuning tool

tools/verify/planetology_sweep.cpp already measures acceptance rate and per-lean cost by sampling seeds. This generalises the same instrument to sample LEAN x BRANCH-COMBINATION space across the whole pipeline (continents through 1900s), not just seeds within the biosphere chain - the explicit ask being 'generate many worlds, to see what targets are best, and how to tweak the overall strategy.' Two outputs, same as today's sweep: (1) a per-lean/per-branch cost table so a dead-end combination shows up as a number (BL-167's 'no lean is a dead end' rule, extended to branches); (2) the target parameter ranges that go into the eventual constants, the same role today's sweep plays for the homeworld floor.

## What stays fixed

- **The BL-051 sibling-pass architecture convention** (six-pass core stays fixed, extensions land as siblings reading the shared generation_record) - continents-as-history is the biggest sibling pass yet, but the convention itself does not change.
- **The eight-line biography cap and 'diagnostic test' from PLANETOLOGY.md** ('for every generated value, name the decision it changes; anything that fails is deleted, not tuned') - applies to every new stage, not just the biosphere chain.
- **Determinism discipline** - per-stage hashed sub-streams, no std::normal_distribution/uniform_int_distribution, no bare transcendentals in gate paths - all of PLANETOLOGY.md's 'Determinism & cost' section applies unchanged to the new stages.
- **BL-167's homeworld rule** - constrain the inputs (via leans/branches), never clamp the gates.

## What needs its own design pass (not settled here)

1. **TILE_GENERATION.md** - the actual plate-simulation model (how continents drift/collide/rift as a function of S3's tectonic-activity roll already computed by planetology; what replaces the six-pass core's heightmap/noise/cluster approach, or whether it becomes an input to that pipeline rather than a full replacement).
2. **NATION_GENERATION.md + CORPORATION_GENERATION.md** - the settlement/industrialisation/1900s simulation itself: what drives a nation's borders, political character and wealth as OUTPUT rather than Voronoi input; how corporate focus emerges from that history rather than an authored table; how this interacts with the economic premise in GENERATION_STRATEGY.md (saturated substrate, specialist corporations) which must survive the rewrite unchanged in spirit.
3. **The checkpoint/branch data model** - where branch state lives (extends planetology_state? a new per-body/per-nation structure?), and its relationship to BL-208's world-history-log (an append-only narrative substrate already design-owed for a different reason - corp/AI action logging - but a plausible shared storage substrate worth checking before inventing a second one).
4. **Cost.** This is explicitly the deepest option at every branch point Ben was offered (continents: replace vs narrate; nations: simulate vs Voronoi+narrate; multi-world: offline tool vs player-facing vs both-with-branch-checkpoints) - each subject-doc design pass should re-surface the cheaper alternative as a comparison point even though the direction is decided, so the cost is visible rather than assumed.

Read GENERATION_STRATEGY.md in full (ordering, economic premise, open cross-doc items), PLANETOLOGY.md 'Known weaknesses' + 'The homeworld rule' + 'Determinism & cost', and BL-051's parked design before starting any subject-doc pass.

items.title: Selection band: retire the click-anchored sticky card for a fixed bottom band, sandwiched between the full-height shell column and right chrome column
items.summary: LANDED 2026-07-28 (Ben session). Discovered mid-session that SELECTION.md/LAYOUT.md were already stale against the actual code: the fold-out-column sidebar they describe had already been superseded by a click-anchored 'sticky card' (BL-194/195/196/200) that freezes at the click position and centres there, clamped to the canvas — THIS was the thing 'floating with the cursor' that Ben's ask targeted. Settled shape (Ben, 2026-07-28): the nav rail, shell fold-out column, and the right chrome column (comms + minimap) all run the FULL SCREEN HEIGHT; the Selection element is a NEW FIXED BAND sandwiched between them at the very bottom — not floating, not click-anchored, not sharing the shell column with the ledgers. Selecting something no longer closes whatever fold-out ledger is open (the two used to be mutually exclusive column occupants; they no longer compete for space at all).
items.design:
SETTLED AND LANDED 2026-07-28. 

## What changed

- **Placement.** `ui::draw_selection_card` (selection_card.cpp) renamed `draw_selection_band`. Removed all click-anchor logic (`ui.card_anchor`, freeze-centre-clamp) — the band now always fills the exact rect the caller passes: `{col_w, disp.y - selection_band_height}` sized `{right_edge - col_w, selection_band_height}`, where `col_w` is the shell column's right edge and `right_edge` is the right chrome column's left edge (both already computed in app.cpp for other chrome). `selection_band_height` (340px, tuned so the tile layout's hex-neighbourhood + accordion chart fit without clipping) is a new named constant in selection_card.hpp.
- **`ui.card_anchor` field removed entirely** from ui_state.hpp, along with its five writers (body_surface_canvas.cpp x2 — click and dwell-open, circumplanetary_canvas.cpp, solar_system_canvas.cpp, construction_panel.cpp, corporation_panel.cpp) — confirmed dead after the rename, removed rather than left as an unused field per the project's 'if certain it's unused, delete it' convention.
- **Selection no longer closes ledgers.** app.cpp's `close_all_panels(m_ui)` call on a new selection (previously required because the sticky card and the fold-out ledgers both wanted the shell column) is removed. The drill-down stack (`card_stack`/`card_resource_page`) still resets on a new selection — that part was never about column contention.
- **Canvas region unchanged.** The primary canvas still draws full-window behind the chrome (LAYOUT.md's existing 'chrome currently occludes the edges' note already covers this) — the band simply occludes the bottom strip the same way the nav rail/header/minimap already occlude their edges. Click-through is prevented the same way it already was for every other chrome window: `io.WantCaptureMouse` gates canvas input globally (app.cpp's `panel_blocking` check), unchanged.
- **Doc-comment sweep.** Every 'sticky card' / 'sticky detail card' reference across the touched files renamed to 'Selection band' so the terminology doesn't keep drifting from the code (charts.hpp, hex_render.hpp, plot_history.hpp, hover_card.hpp, selection_panel.hpp, app.hpp, app.cpp, body_surface_canvas.cpp).

## Verified

Visually via `scripts/verify/selection_band.lua` (capture-only, no golden yet): (1) a nav-rail ledger (Economy panel) open in the shell column AND a building selection open in the bottom band simultaneously — confirms both the fixed placement and the no-longer-mutually-exclusive behaviour; (2) a bare tile selection, confirming the taller band (340px, up from an initial too-tight 260px) gives the hex-neighbourhood render and the per-resource production chart room to not clip. Regression-checked: `determinism_harness` and `world_audit` still green (this item is UI-only, touches no `world/*` logic).

## Not done

- **SELECTION.md / LAYOUT.md text itself** — both still describe the pre-BL-194 fold-out-sidebar shape as if it were current; this item's `authority_doc` update is the next immediate step, not yet written at the time this entry was filed.
- **Golden images** for the new capture — capture-only for now.
- **Facts-column placement** — Ben confirmed only the zoomed view + action buttons move to the band; muted decision-facts (profitability, activity pulse, Thrives/Valid) were assumed to stay wherever `draw_selection_content` already puts them (today: inside the same band, since the whole per-kind content — action AND facts — renders through one shared builder). Revisit if the band ever needs to split Facts back out to the column.

## FOLLOW-UP, same session 2026-07-28: the tile layout reshaped to 3 columns

Ben's next ask, once he saw the band live: reshape the TILE kind's internal layout (the one kind with its own bespoke layout, BL-123) into three horizontal columns spanning the band — left 1/4 zoomed hex view, centre 1/2 a paged metric accordion, right 1/4 a bigger action-button grid. Landed:

- **Centre accordion widened in SCOPE, not just size.** Previously paged through deposited resources only; now also pages the tile's own `habitability`/`hazard_level` scalars (vs. this body's average) so a barren tile still has content. Atmospheric pollution / per-tile population are NOT modelled today — deliberately not faked as pages. Only resource pages are click-drillable (habitability/hazard have no time-series history tracked).
- **Action grid: 3x2 tried first, corrected to 2x3.** Ben's literal spec ("3 by 2 grid") produced 38px-wide button slivers, not "bigger" — the quarter-width column was too narrow for 3 across. Asked Ben directly rather than guessing further (per [[ben-imprecise-instruction-ask-dont-guess]], the memory this exchange produced); he picked 2 columns x 3 rows, same 6 slots (4 real actions + 2 reserved), chunkier buttons.
- **`shell_column_width` narrowed** from BL-124's `[480,576]` to `[380,460]` (factor 0.272->0.20) to widen the band further, per Ben's explicit follow-up ("widen the whole board") after initially being offered it as the higher-risk alternative and declining. Justification: BL-124's widening was explicitly to host the Selection sidebar, which no longer lives in that column at all post-BL-213 — the extra width had no remaining purpose there. Verified other ledgers (Economy panel checked visually) still read fine at the narrower width; `determinism_harness`/`world_audit` still green (UI-only). The right chrome column (minimap/comms/time, `mm_w`) was deliberately left untouched — its enlargement served unrelated legibility goals, not Selection.
- Both `SELECTION.md` § The tile element's layout and `LAYOUT.md` § The shell column updated to match.

items.design:
NOT YET SETTLED. Scope and open questions, to be resolved in its own design pass (per the doc-by-doc sign-off pattern this session used for BL-210):

## What already exists to build on

- **The developer-facing ledger is fully designed** (GENERATION_LEDGER.md): a per-tile derivation breadcrumb (height -> ocean -> band/moisture -> composition -> landform -> deposits) and per-body summaries (composition/landform histograms, key thresholds, profile echo), regenerated on demand from `generation_record` rather than persisted.
- **Planetology's eight-line biography** (PLANETOLOGY.md 'Presentation') is the textual convention this ledger should extend, not replace: dated lines, two columns (what happened / what it left behind), asymmetric length (a Cradle gets eight lines, a dead world gets three), homeworld-relative units. `continents.hpp`'s `history_event` struct already reuses this exact shape (chain_stage::engine lines) — this item's job is giving those lines, and the ones Nations/Corporations will eventually emit, an actual place to be READ.
- **MENU.md's History slot is already settled as the destination** — gated by exploration (BL-067's survey fog), a distinct informational set from a live event log, gives 'post-generation advisory' on resource/workforce state.

## What needs deciding

1. **Scope for THIS pass vs. later passes.** BL-210 has so far only landed Continents/Drift; Biosphere (Planetology) already has its full biography; Nations/Corporations don't exist yet as causal-consequence output. Does the History slot ship incrementally (biosphere biography first, since it's already fully built and just needs a UI home) or wait for the whole BL-210 chain?
2. **One long narrative per body, or per-nation/per-corp sub-views once those land?** The existing biography is per-body. Once Nations/Corporations become oral-history outputs (BL-210's remaining scope), does History gain a nation tab, a corp tab, or does everything stay nested under its body?
2b. **Exploration-gating interaction.** A body's Continents/Drift and Biosphere history should probably be visible once surveyed (matches the existing 'Air must show full history at campaign start' exception PLANETOLOGY.md already carries for the homeworld) — but Nations/Corporations history may need its own gate (DISCOVERY.md's activity fog?) since it is about *current* political/economic actors, not dead geology.
3. **Shared content builder or a new one?** GENERATION_LEDGER.md already commits the per-tile breadcrumb to a shared builder (ledger panel / hover card / Selection element all call it, per SELECTION.md). Should the biography text follow the same shared-builder discipline (so a future 'why does this nation have this ideology' hover reuses the same text as the History panel), or is prose long-form enough that it only ever renders in one place?
4. **Render surface.** `src/ui/charts.{hpp,cpp}` already exists for bar-chart-style summaries (reused across the Planetology wizard and tile-selection deposit graphs) — the History slot's per-body summaries should reuse it rather than inventing new chart code. The dated-line biography itself is plain text, so no new charting need there.

Read GENERATION_LEDGER.md in full (especially § Open items 'Player-facing variant') and MENU.md's History slot entry before starting this design pass.

items.summary: DESIGN-OWED 2026-07-28 (Ben session, playtest follow-up). Ben's call: 'anonymise a lot of the chat log (only nations speak, and they pretend it is their own voice)' — the Public comms channel should never show an individual corporation's message; every public post is attributed to a NATION, voiced in the first person, standing in for whatever its registered corporations actually did. This is the EXACT SHAPE of the already-settled competitor-visibility rule (DISCOVERY.md: 'Rival internals are private... market supply/demand aggregates and prices are public — the deliberate signal. The player reasons over public signals, not handed over'), extended from the market channel to the comms channel. Today's Public channel opens with a placeholder epoch line only (BL-205, app.cpp:672-675: '<N> corporations on the public channel') — the real per-corp message generation is the corp_ai/persona-pack layer (BL-202/BL-207, persona::pack's in-voice claim/explanation strings), which currently has no notion of a nation-level mouthpiece at all.
items.design:
NOT YET SETTLED. Open questions for its own design pass:

## The pattern this extends

DISCOVERY.md already settled the general shape: private detail (rival production/stockpiles) stays hidden; a public AGGREGATE signal (market prices/supply-demand) is what the player actually reasons over. This item is that same rule applied to comms instead of markets: corp-level chatter (whatever corp_ai/persona_pack generates per-corp today) becomes the PRIVATE layer; a nation-level statement is the only thing that ever reaches the Public channel, and it is phrased as if the nation itself is speaking, not reporting on a corporation.

## What needs deciding

1. **Aggregation rule.** When multiple corporations registered in the same nation act in a way that would generate a persona message, how does that collapse into ONE national statement? Loudest/most consequential action wins? A running digest? Does a quiet tick produce no national message at all (silence is fine — 'ledgers-start-closed' convention already used elsewhere)?
2. **Voice source.** `persona::pack` already produces in-voice claim/explanation strings (<=140 chars) per persona — is a NATION now a persona (its `ideology`/`expansionism`/`economic_focus` from NATION_GENERATION.md Pass 4 become the voice), replacing or wrapping the corp-level persona? Note NATION_GENERATION.md Pass 4's ideology/expansionism are currently a random draw, not a consequence (the same gap BL-210's Nations rewrite is targeting) — this item may want to wait on that, or may motivate doing it sooner.
3. **Does the underlying corp-level chatter still exist anywhere?** Fully deleted, or does it become the 'private' layer visible only to the corp's own player/rival-audit surfaces (symmetric with market private/public split)? If kept, where does a curious player ever see it (a corp dossier? nothing at all, matching 'rival internals are private... never appear')?
4. **Interaction with the History Ledger (BL-211).** A nation's public voice is a live, ongoing signal; the History Ledger is retrospective generation record. Likely disjoint surfaces (comms = present-tense play, History = how-we-got-here), but worth confirming they don't want to be the same panel.
5. **Beliefs dependency.** Out of scope here per this session's standing note ([[ben-generation-consequences-not-simulation]]) — Beliefs (Fable's) may eventually flavour a nation's voice, but this item should not block on it; a nation's voice can start from the existing ideology/expansionism/economic_focus attributes alone.

Read DISCOVERY.md in full (especially the competitor-visibility rule this generalises), corp_ai.hpp/persona_pack.hpp (the existing per-corp voice mechanism), and NATION_GENERATION.md Pass 4 (today's ideology/expansionism draw) before starting this design pass.

items.title: Drill-through as a common concept - one progressive-disclosure idiom every dense surface obeys, so a compact read is the default and depth is asked for
items.summary: Raised by Ben on seeing the BL-211 History ledger land (2026-07-29): 'This is fantastic... compact and readable. HOWEVER, for many people it would be information overload.' The History ledger is the case in point - three round tabs over ten stage accordions, each holding two to four charts plus two paragraphs of physics. It is legible because Ben already read that chain once in the wizard; a player who has not is handed a wall. The ask is NOT to cut the depth. It is to make drill-through a CONCEPT the whole UI shares - a compact top layer everywhere, depth reached by an explicit uniform gesture - rather than a per-surface decision each ledger re-invents.
items.design:
NOT YET DESIGNED - captured per Rule 0a, high priority, to be designed in its own pass.

## The problem

Depth keeps arriving as *more surface*, because every surface decides its own disclosure independently:
- the History ledger (BL-211) opens on a stage explainer plus its charts;
- the tile Selection band (BL-123) pages an accordion of every deposited resource;
- the wizard (BL-167) shows ten stages of gates whether or not the player wants them;
- the Corporation dashboard's four roll-ups "click through into the relevant per-system ledger" (MENU.md slot 1) - a fourth, different idiom.

Each is individually defensible; together they are four answers to one question. A player learns the gesture once per surface instead of once.

## What already exists to build on

- **BL-196 (designed, v0.1.1)** - recursive drill-down: elements inside a card open CHILD cards, bounded by acyclicity. That is the *mechanism* for one family of surfaces. This item is the *concept* BL-196 should be an instance of, not a competitor to it - sequence them together, or fold BL-196 in.
- **The card-drilldown UX notes (2026-07-23)** - affordance, breadcrumb, expand-not-replace. Those three are probably the concept's core rules already.
- **LAYOUT.md's nine-container vocabulary (BL-141)** - the precedent for exactly this kind of closed-set answer. Drill-through wants the same treatment: a closed set of disclosure levels, not a spectrum.
- **SELECTION.md's action|facts split plus its go-to** - the existing "summary here, reference one hop away" rule; the ledger family is its other half.

## What needs deciding

1. **How many levels, and what are they called?** A plausible three: GLANCE (a figure and its direction - the header, a card's fact line), READ (the compact composed view - what the History ledger's Chain tab is now), STUDY (the full derivation - explainers, per-tile breadcrumbs, the wizard's own framing). Is three right, and must every surface place itself on that ladder?
2. **What is the uniform gesture?** Expand in place, a child card (BL-196), or a go-to into a deeper surface - and must the same gesture mean the same thing everywhere, or is the RULE only that each level advertises itself the same way?
3. **What is the default level per surface, and is it remembered?** The History Chain currently opens the round's first stage expanded; the honest default is probably GLANCE everywhere, with the player's last chosen depth remembered per surface.
4. **Does the wizard participate?** It is the one surface where full depth on first contact is arguably right - it IS "the first thing a player sees" (BL-167). If it is exempt, say so explicitly rather than by omission.
5. **Text density is part of this.** The stage explainers are two paragraphs of real chemistry. At GLANCE they should probably not render at all rather than be truncated - which couples this item to BL-215 (wrap/precision) without being the same question.

## Non-goals

Cutting content. Ben's framing is explicitly that the compact read is good and the depth is worth keeping - this is about WHEN the depth appears, not WHETHER.

items.title: Render-precision audit - walk every UI element and confirm text wraps rather than clips, at the smallest supported display
items.summary: Raised by Ben 2026-07-29 alongside BL-211: 'the other mistake is that text does not wrap fully. We need to go through UI elements and double check things render with precision, leaving text to wrap on smaller monitors.' Concrete instances found while building the History ledger: chart TITLES clip mid-word in the fold-out column ('Metals (homeworld endowment, 1.0 ='); chart LEGEND rows clip their value ('Agricultural Produce 0'); the stage accordion header clipped its question until it was shortened to the stage name; the biography's consequence lines clipped until switched to TextWrapped. Each was fixed or dodged locally - this item is the systematic pass.
items.design:
NOT YET DESIGNED - captured per Rule 0a. High priority: this is a correctness class, not a polish class. Silent truncation of a load-bearing figure is ALREADY banned by LAYOUT.md's container vocabulary; the instances above are that ban being broken in practice.

## Why it recurs

LAYOUT.md section "Container vocabulary" (BL-141) already settles the rule: nine containers, each with exactly ONE text policy (wrap, or guaranteed-fit), and "silent truncation is never acceptable" for a load-bearing figure. What is missing is enforcement. Nothing checks that a widget honours its container's policy, so every new surface re-litigates it by eye - and gets it right at the width it was authored against, which is the developer's monitor.

## Scope for the pass

1. **Enumerate** every drawing site against LAYOUT.md's nine containers and record which policy each claims.
2. **Test at the floor, not at the desk.** The shell column is width-derived (shell_column_width, ~380px at 1720 with a 380 floor); the smallest supported display should be STATED in DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES (Display environment) and then actually captured, not assumed.
3. **Fix by policy, not by shortening the string.** A clipped chart title wants a wrapping title or a measured box - not a shorter title, which loses information and drifts back the moment someone edits it.
4. **charts.cpp is the worst offender and the best test case.** It hand-draws every label into a fixed screen-space box: titles, tick labels, legend rows and threshold captions all assume room they may not have. A narrow-host chart mode (legend BELOW the plot rather than beside it) is the likely fix, and would also unsqueeze the History ledger's plots.

## Open questions

- **What is the smallest supported display?** 1280x720 is the verify harness window and the options-menu floor preset - is that the contract?
- **Can this be CHECKED rather than eyeballed?** A verify script capturing every panel at the floor resolution makes the pass repeatable; whether clipping can be detected automatically (vs. eyeballed per capture) is the interesting question. Per CLAUDE.md (Tool creation is skill creation), prefer the saved check over a one-time sweep.
- **Relationship to BL-063 (accessibility / legibility baseline)** - overlapping remit; reconcile or merge before promoting.

items.title: Shell re-plan - move the comms log to the bottom-left corner and give the freed centre-right band back to pinned items
items.summary: Raised by Ben 2026-07-29, immediately after BL-213 put the Selection band along the bottom: 'it could be worth moving the chat log to the bottom left corner. This will make it look a bit better with our selection element / menu both wanting that space. We can refactor the pinned items back to the centre right space.' Two moves in one: comms leaves the right chrome column for the bottom-left, and the band it vacates (right edge, between the time panel and the minimap) returns to PINNED ITEMS - the affordance the Explorer placeholder reserved before the comms log replaced it on 2026-07-26.
items.design:
NOT YET DESIGNED - captured per Rule 0a. Ben's phrasing is a direction, not a layout spec; the geometry must be settled WITH HIM before anything moves (see Open questions - do not guess the rect).

## The observation behind it

BL-213 put the Selection band along the bottom, between the full-height shell column and the full-height right chrome column. The bottom-left corner is now the junction of three things that all want it: the shell column's fold-out ledger (which runs to the bottom margin), the Selection band's left edge, and the nav rail. Ben's read is that the corner collects more attention than it earns, and that comms belongs there.

## What the move buys

- **Comms is ambient.** It is a read-when-you-notice-it surface (nation-voiced public chatter, BL-212), not a decision surface. The bottom-left is the right weight for it; the right edge - directly under the time panel, above the minimap - is prime space it does not need.
- **Pinned items get a home again.** LAYOUT.md records that pinning "was never wired; if it returns it will be a chat-adjacent affordance". This reopens it: pinned items as a first-class centre-right surface (EXPLORER.md's original reservation), which is where a player would want a watched market / body / building parked while working elsewhere.

## Open questions - ASK BEN, DO NOT GUESS

1. **Does comms sit INSIDE the shell column (below the fold-out ledger), or in its own rect left of the Selection band?** These look alike in a sketch and are very different to build: the first shares the column's width and scroll; the second is a fourth region and pushes the Selection band's left edge right.
2. **What happens to the fold-out ledger's height?** It runs to the bottom margin today. If comms takes the bottom-left, the ledger stops short - re-tuning every ledger's vertical budget (the BL-117 one-question-per-view splits were sized against the full column).
3. **What ARE pinned items, concretely?** Never designed. A pinned entity is presumably a Selection-band content builder rendered in a persistent slot - the same per-kind dispatcher, hosted twice. How many pins, how one is added (a pin button on the band header beside go-to and close), and whether pins survive a session are all open.
4. **Does the minimap move?** It anchors bottom-right today. If pinned items take the centre-right, the minimap and its lens bar keep the corner, but the right column's vertical budget splits three ways instead of two.

## Sequencing

Behind BL-215 (a layout re-plan landing before the wrap audit just gives the audit more to re-check), and probably behind BL-214, whose disclosure levels decide how much a pinned item shows.

items.title: Checkpoint/branch data model - where branch state lives and how a lean biases which branch fires (BL-210 split 1 of 3)
items.summary: Split out of BL-210's umbrella design (2026-07-31) as the first of three subject-doc passes it named as not-yet-settled. Extends BL-167's shipped preferences mechanism (eight axes, each a lean of any/low/mid/high, resolved by reject-and-reroll) so a lean can also bias WHICH branch fires at a checkpoint, not just narrow a sampling range within one round. Two checkpoint classes exist in the pipeline today only as narration: the mass-extinction branch (already dated in the S5-S8 biosphere biography, e.g. '252 Mya extinction') and the new historical-extinction branch (collapse/war/revolution at the settlement stage, BL-218's biggest new idea). Neither is wired to the lean system yet - both are pure classification with no bias hook.
items.design:
NOT YET SETTLED - this entry scopes the design pass, it does not close it. Read BL-210's full design field, PLANETOLOGY.md's preferences model (Round A/B/C, reject-and-reroll), and BL-208 (world-history-log, design-owed, v0.3.0) before designing.

## Open questions (carried and sharpened from BL-210)

1. **Where does branch state live?** Candidates: (a) extend `planetology_state` (today per-body, biosphere-scoped) to carry a generic checkpoint/branch list; (b) a new per-body structure parallel to it; (c) defer to BL-208's world-history-log once that lands, treating each checkpoint as a logged event with a branch tag rather than inventing separate storage. (c) is cheapest if BL-208's timeline allows it, but BL-208 is v0.3.0-scoped and this item is post-v0.1.0 - check whether checkpoint data can live provisionally in (a) and migrate to BL-208's log once it exists, rather than blocking on it.
2. **How does a lean bias a branch choice without becoming a probability slider?** BL-167's rule ('if you have preferences you can find them, but really you don't get full customization') must hold: reject-and-reroll stays the mechanism, a lean only narrows which branches are eligible to be proposed, never assigns them a visible weight.
3. **What counts as a checkpoint?** At minimum: the existing mass-extinction points (S5-S8) and the new historical-extinction point (settlement stage, BL-218). Confirm no additional checkpoints are needed before the two rewrites below start consuming this model - retrofitting a third checkpoint class after BL-218/BL-219 design lands is more expensive than settling the shape now.
4. **Viability floors.** Every branch must still fail against a homeworld-viability floor (BL-167's pattern) and reroll on failure - confirm this generalises cleanly or needs a per-checkpoint floor definition.

Does NOT need to settle: the specific historical-extinction branch outcomes themselves (that's BL-218's design), or the batch-sweep tool extension (an execution-depth follow-on once this model and BL-218/219 are settled, not a fourth design item).

items.title: Nations rewrite - territory, political character & wealth as outputs of a simulated settlement/industrialisation history, not Voronoi + random draw (BL-210 split 2 of 3)
items.summary: Split out of BL-210 (2026-07-31); per DEVLOG (2026-07-28) named as 'the biggest remaining piece' of the whole pivot. Replaces NATION_GENERATION.md's Pass 1-5 (Voronoi BFS seed/growth/merge, then an independently-random Pass 4 politics draw) with a settlement -> industrialisation -> 1900s stage: nation borders, ideology/expansionism/economic_focus, and resource-profile emphasis become OUTPUTS of a simulated history seeded by the continent/biosphere chain above (arable share, river connectivity, ore provinces, fossil geography - BL-210/BL-209's chains) rather than summed post-hoc from tiles or drawn independently at random. Directly answers PLANETOLOGY.md's own named gap: 'the pass hands nothing to nation or corporation generation... this is the largest missing connection.' This is where the 'historical extinction' checkpoint (BL-217) fires, and where the post-WW2 industrial grounding open item (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md, CORPORATION_GENERATION.md) finally gets a mechanism.
items.design:
NOT YET SETTLED. Read NATION_GENERATION.md in full (current Pass 1-5), GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's economic premise (saturated substrate, resource-carved markets - this must survive the rewrite unchanged in spirit), and BL-217 once settled (where checkpoint/branch state lives) before designing.

## What must survive the rewrite

- **The economic premise** (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md): a saturated, earth-like base the Nation AI owns as background, resource-carved markets (BL-096). The rewrite changes HOW a nation's territory/character/wealth are derived, not the shape of what the economy does with them afterward.
- **Non-Kepler scope**: nation generation still runs only where habitable area justifies it (Kepler only, prototype).
- **Determinism discipline**: per-stage hashed sub-streams, no bare transcendentals, the homeworld rule (constrain inputs, never clamp outputs) - same as every other stage in the chain.

## Open questions

1. **What replaces Pass 1-2 (seed placement + Voronoi BFS)?** A settlement-emergence model presumably seeds population centres on high-arable/high-river-connectivity tiles first (the continent/biosphere chain's own outputs), then grows territory as a consequence of historical competition rather than a pure geometric expansion. How much of the existing BFS/growth-weight machinery (Pass 1b/2, already tuned for size variance - BL-053) is reused vs replaced is a real cost question BL-210 asks to keep visible.
2. **What replaces Pass 4 (political character)?** Ideology/expansionism/economic_focus should emerge from the settlement/industrialisation history (a nation that industrialised early and had resource competition with a neighbour becomes 'expansionist', for instance) rather than an independent random draw. Needs a concrete derivation rule, not just a direction.
2a. **How does the historical-extinction checkpoint (BL-217) actually alter a nation's history?** - collapse, war, revolution as concrete effects on territory/character, not just a narrated line.
3. **Fragmentation.** NATION_GENERATION.md's open item on real historical fragmentation (exclaves, disputed zones - parked BL-054) may be substantially answered for free by a real settlement-history sim; confirm whether BL-054 folds into this item or stays separately parked.
4. **Cost comparison.** Per BL-210's own discipline, re-surface the cheaper alternative (keep Voronoi + richer narration only) as a comparison point even though Ben has already picked the deeper option three times running.

Does NOT need to settle: corporation industrial-focus derivation (BL-219, which consumes this item's output once settled).

items.title: Corporations rewrite - industrial focus as an emergent output of nation settlement history, not an authored focus table (BL-210 split 3 of 3)
items.summary: Split out of BL-210 (2026-07-31), the third and smallest of the three subject-doc passes - deliberately sequenced last since it consumes BL-218's nation-history output. Replaces CORPORATION_GENERATION.md's Pass 1-2 (nation assignment weighted by static economic_focus, then an independently-weighted focus draw) with focus/holdings that read as a plausible consequence of the home nation's settlement/industrialisation history, rather than a table lookup. Directly answers the two open items CORPORATION_GENERATION.md already names: 'post-WW2 industrial grounding for the asset mix' and, partially, 'nation-seeded privatisation'.
items.design:
NOT YET SETTLED. Read CORPORATION_GENERATION.md in full (current Pass 1-4, the 'specialists not full-chain industrialists' premise, and every item under its own Open items section), and BL-218 once settled, before designing.

## What must survive the rewrite

- **Corporations stay specialists** (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's economic premise) - lean, focus-coherent holdings, not a broad spread. This item changes WHY a corp has the focus it has, not the lean-holdings shape itself (that shape is separately load-bearing and already tuned).
- **Player corporation parity** - the player's corp is generated by the same pipeline as every rival, no special-cased generation rules (current invariant, stated in both NATION_GENERATION.md and CORPORATION_GENERATION.md).

## Open questions

1. **What in the nation's settlement history determines a corp's focus?** E.g. a nation whose settlement history shows early heavy industrialisation around ore provinces should tend to emit extraction/processing-focused corporations; a nation whose history reads as trade-hub/coastal should emit trade-focused ones. Needs a concrete derivation, not just plausibility.
2. **Does this retire the authored focus-weighting table entirely, or keep it as a fallback/tunable bias on top of the emergent signal?** A pure emergent derivation risks losing the 'diversity without enforcing a strict quota' property Pass 2 currently guarantees by construction.
3. **Post-WW2 industrial grounding** (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md's own open item) - this is the mechanism that item has been waiting for; the design pass should name which real-world industrial patterns (post-war extraction-to-manufacturing pipelines) the asset-mix derivation is modelled on, not treat it as automatically solved by 'derive from history'.
4. **Nation-seeded privatisation** (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md's own open item) - check whether this rewrite naturally produces a hook for nations seeding corporations into underserved industries, or whether that stays a separate follow-on.

Once this item and BL-218 are both settled and BUILT, BL-210's remaining scope (batch-sweep tool extension to lean x branch-combination space, and propagating the whole pivot into TILE_GENERATION.md/NATION_GENERATION.md/CORPORATION_GENERATION.md as settled authority) closes the umbrella.
